objects.description: No custom types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) are defined in this header. The file provides a single static inline function PerfettoFnv1a implementing a 64-bit FNV-1a hash. All referenced types (uint64_t, size_t, uint8_t) are from standard headers. Therefore there are no data types to document.
Enumeration of protobuf wire types used when encoding/decoding field tags in serialized protobuf messages.
Packed message helper for serializing protobuf packed repeated uint64 fields. Wraps a PerfettoPbMsg to enable zero-copy nested message encoding.
Packed message helper for protobuf packed repeated uint32 fields, using varint encoding.
Packed message helper for protobuf packed repeated int64 fields, varint-encoded (two's complement cast to uint64).
Packed message helper for protobuf packed repeated int32 fields, varint-encoded (cast to uint64).
Packed message helper for protobuf packed repeated sint64 fields, zig-zag encoded then varint.
Packed message helper for protobuf packed repeated sint32 fields, zig-zag encoded then varint.
Packed message helper for protobuf packed repeated fixed64 fields, little-endian 64-bit fixed width.
Packed message helper for protobuf packed repeated fixed32 fields, little-endian 32-bit fixed width.
Packed message helper for protobuf packed repeated sfixed64 (signed fixed 64-bit) fields; bytes copied as 64-bit payload then appended as fixed64.
Packed message helper for protobuf packed repeated sfixed32 (signed fixed 32-bit) fields; bytes copied then appended as fixed32.
Packed message helper for protobuf packed repeated double fields; value reinterpreted to 64-bit and written as fixed64.
Packed message helper for protobuf packed repeated float fields; value reinterpreted to 32-bit and written as fixed32.
Wrapper owning/holding a PerfettoStreamWriter used as the byte sink for protobuf message encoding helpers in this header. It provides the writer field that PerfettoPbMsg uses to append bytes.

State object used while constructing a protobuf-encoded message. Tracks the output writer, accumulated message size, and bookkeeping for a pre-reserved length field and nested/parent relationships when building length-delimited (type 2) submessages.

Iterator helper struct for parsing protobuf messages using the Perfetto public PB decoder. Holds a decoder cursor and the most recently parsed field. Iterate by initializing with PerfettoPbDecoderIterateBegin or PerfettoPbDecoderIterateNestedBegin and advancing with PerfettoPbDecoderIterateNext. The inner types (PerfettoPbDecoder, PerfettoPbDecoderField) are defined in included headers and are not defined here.

Opaque struct representing a streaming writer context used by the inline helpers in this header. It is referenced as struct PerfettoStreamWriter and is defined externally in perfetto/public/abi/stream_writer_abi.h. Its fields used here include begin, end, write_ptr, and written_previously. As this header only provides inline helper functions, the concrete layout and lifecycle are defined in the ABI header. Details such as construction/destruction are unknown in this file.
Opaque tracing session implementation type. Only forward-declared elsewhere; this header references it but does not define it. Purpose: represents a tracing session handle for Perfetto backends.

Enumeration type representing backend selection for Perfetto tracing (e.g., in-process, system). This header references it via parameter but does not define it; it is defined in perfetto/public/abi/backend_type.h.

Initialization arguments for the global Perfetto producer. Contains the target backends bitmask and an optional shared-memory size hint (in KB). The struct is not ABI-stable; fields may change across versions. backends uses PerfettoBackendTypes (defined elsewhere). shmem_size_hint_kb should be a multiple of 4KB and may be capped or ignored by the implementation.

Category object used by Perfetto Track Event to represent a tracing category. This header does not provide the full type definition of struct PerfettoTeCategory; it constructs/defines category instances via macros that assume the real struct definition is provided by perfetto/public/track_event.h. The initializer fields suggest the struct contains: an atomic-enabled flag pointer, an optional descriptor pointer, an inline descriptor with name, description, tags array pointer, and tag count, plus a reserved/flags field. Exact layout is defined externally.

Array type usage for registries of PerfettoTeCategory pointers. Not a separately defined type in this header; shown here only to note that registration macros construct arrays of struct PerfettoTeCategory*. No standalone typedef is defined.
Small POD used by the PERFETTO_TE_* macros to pass an event name and a type tag to the high‑level Track Event emission implementation.

Represents a Perfetto data source type registered with the global producer. Holds an atomic enabled flag shared across threads and an opaque implementation pointer (PerfettoDsImpl) managed by the ABI. Users allocate one per data source type and register it, then iterate active instances for tracing.

Holds optional callbacks and parameters for registering a Perfetto data source type, including lifecycle and TLS/incremental-state hooks, a user argument, buffer exhaustion policy, and stop-ack behavior. Use PerfettoDsParamsDefault() to obtain a zeroed/default-initialized instance.
Opaque iterator wrapper for enumerating active instances of a Perfetto data source on the current thread. Used with PerfettoDsTraceIterateBegin/Next/Break and PERFETTO_DS_TRACE macros.
Helper aggregate used while emitting a TracePacket into a data source instance. It bundles a protobuf writer and the root TracePacket message handle. Use with PerfettoDsTracerPacketBegin/End.

Registered track event category handle holding enablement flag, implementation pointer, public descriptor, and its interned-id (iid). Must be registered before use; unregistering invalidates it for tracing.
Wrapper for a registered track. Contains implementation state including serialized TrackDescriptor buffer, size, and UUID inside impl.
Opaque flow identifier used to link events (intra- or inter-process). Created via helpers that scope the id appropriately.
Low-level iterator over active data source instances for a category on the current thread. Wraps ABI iterator state.
Helper context for interning within a TracePacket. Lazily begins and ends the InternedData submessage and provides access to incremental state.
Thread identifier type used by Perfetto utilities. It is referenced here but defined in perfetto/public/abi/thread_utils_abi.h, not in this header. No definition is present in this file.

objects.description: Opaque heap-backed buffer used with PerfettoStreamWriter to serialize protobuf data. This header only forward-declares the struct; its layout is hidden. Create with PerfettoHeapBufferCreate, copy out data with PerfettoHeapBufferCopyInto, and destroy with PerfettoHeapBufferDestroy. Internal details and lifetime rules beyond these functions are not documented here.

Opaque decoder state for iterating through a protobuf-encoded message stored in a contiguous memory buffer. Holds the current read position and the end pointer. Callers initialize read_ptr/end_ptr to the message bounds and then use the provided API to parse or skip fields; the functions update read_ptr.
Status codes returned by parsing operations to indicate success with more data, completion at end of buffer, or an error where the read pointer was not advanced.
Holds the start pointer and length of a length-delimited (wire type 2) protobuf field within the source buffer. Does not own memory; lifetime tied to the source buffer.

Represents a single parsed protobuf field. Carries a status (as uint32_t corresponding to PerfettoPbDecoderStatus), a wire type (uint32_t; PerfettoPbWireType is referenced but not defined here), the field number, and the decoded value in a union appropriate to the wire type. Memory for delimited fields references the original buffer.

objects.definition: struct PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgs;
objects.description: Opaque/incomplete struct used to hold initialization parameters for a Perfetto producer backend. This header only provides a forward declaration; the layout and fields are intentionally hidden and defined elsewhere. Instances are created/destroyed and configured via the provided C API before initializing a system or in-process producer.

objects.definition: struct PerfettoStreamWriterImpl;
objects.description: Opaque forward-declared implementation object for the protozero stream writer. It hides internal state from public API consumers. No layout or lifetime details are exposed here.

Public stream writer handle owning a writable memory chunk for building protozero-encoded data. Tracks current chunk bounds (begin/end), the current write pointer, and cumulative bytes written in prior chunks. The impl field points to an internal implementation object. Construction and lifetime management are not defined here; users interact via the provided API functions to update write position, request new chunks, append or reserve bytes, and annotate patches for post-chunk backfilling.

Platform-dependent typedef naming the thread identifier type used by the Perfetto SDK. It aliases the native thread ID type for the current platform: pid_t on Linux/NaCl, zx_koid_t on Fuchsia, uint64_t on Apple/Windows, or pthread_t otherwise. Used with PerfettoGetThreadIdImpl() to retrieve the current thread's id.

objects.definition: struct PerfettoTracingSessionImpl;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a Perfetto tracing session. The struct is forward-declared here and implemented elsewhere; it represents the internal session state managed by the Perfetto SDK. Use the provided API functions to create, configure, start/stop, flush, read, and destroy a session. Do not access fields directly (none are exposed). Lifetime is managed by the caller: create via the factory functions and destroy with PerfettoTracingSessionDestroy.

functions.name: PerfettoFnv1a
functions.signature: static inline uint64_t PerfettoFnv1a(const void* data, size_t size)
functions.description: Computes the 64-bit FNV-1a hash of a byte buffer. Call with a pointer to the buffer and its size in bytes; the function iterates over each byte and returns the 64-bit hash value. Suitable for fast, deterministic hashing of raw data; thread-safe and has no side effects. If size is 0, the function returns the FNV-1a offset basis without reading data.
requirements: data must point to at least size bytes of readable memory.
data may be null only when size == 0 (the buffer is not accessed in that case).
size is the number of bytes to hash (non-negative; passed as size_t).
The function performs no allocation and no I/O; callers should not expect error reporting aside from the returned value.

functions.name: PerfettoPbMakeTag
functions.signature: static inline uint32_t PerfettoPbMakeTag(int32_t field_id, enum PerfettoPbWireType wire_type)
functions.description: Constructs a protobuf field tag by combining a field number and a wire type (wire_type in the low 3 bits, field_id in the remaining high bits). Use when emitting protobuf field headers before field payloads.
requirements: wire_type must be a valid enum PerfettoPbWireType value
field_id must be representable in the tag format (left-shift by 3 without overflow of the 32-bit result); typical protobuf practice is a non-negative field number
No null pointer requirements (pure value operation)

functions.name: PerfettoPbWriteVarInt
functions.signature: static inline uint8_t* PerfettoPbWriteVarInt(uint64_t value, uint8_t* dst)
functions.description: Encodes value as a protobuf varint into the buffer at dst and returns a pointer to the first byte after the written varint. Intended for serializing varint-encoded fields.
requirements: dst must be non-null
dst must point to writable memory with enough space to hold the encoded varint; up to PERFETTO_PB_VARINT_MAX_SIZE_64 (10) bytes for a 64-bit value
The caller must use the returned pointer as the new write position

functions.name: PerfettoPbWriteFixed32
functions.signature: static inline uint8_t* PerfettoPbWriteFixed32(uint32_t value, uint8_t* buf)
functions.description: Writes value as a 4-byte little-endian fixed32 into buf and returns buf + 4. Used for protobuf fixed32 fields.
requirements: buf must be non-null
buf must point to writable memory with at least 4 bytes available
The caller should use the returned pointer as the next write position

functions.name: PerfettoPbWriteFixed64
functions.signature: static inline uint8_t* PerfettoPbWriteFixed64(uint64_t value, uint8_t* buf)
functions.description: Writes value as an 8-byte little-endian fixed64 into buf and returns buf + 8. Used for protobuf fixed64/sfixed64/double fields (after appropriate bit-casting for floating types).
requirements: buf must be non-null
buf must point to writable memory with at least 8 bytes available
The caller should use the returned pointer as the next write position

functions.name: PerfettoPbParseVarInt
functions.signature: static inline const uint8_t* PerfettoPbParseVarInt(const uint8_t* start, const uint8_t* end, uint64_t* out_value)
functions.description: Parses a protobuf varint from the buffer range [start, end). On success, stores the decoded value in out_value and returns a pointer to the first unconsumed byte. If the varint is incomplete (not enough bytes in the range), returns start and sets out_value to 0.
requirements: start and end must be valid pointers defining a readable contiguous range with start <= end
out_value must be non-null
Caller must check the return value: success iff return > start; failure/incomplete iff return == start
The input must contain a well-formed varint; overlong/invalid encodings may cause the function to return start (failure)

functions.name: PerfettoPbZigZagEncode32
functions.signature: static inline uint32_t PerfettoPbZigZagEncode32(int32_t value)
functions.description: ZigZag-encodes a 32-bit signed integer to a 32-bit unsigned integer, mapping small negative numbers to small unsigned values suitable for varint encoding in protobuf (sint32).
requirements: No special preconditions beyond value being a 32-bit signed integer
Pure computation; no side effects

functions.name: PerfettoPbZigZagEncode64
functions.signature: static inline uint64_t PerfettoPbZigZagEncode64(int64_t value)
functions.description: ZigZag-encodes a 64-bit signed integer to a 64-bit unsigned integer for efficient varint encoding in protobuf (sint64).
requirements: No special preconditions beyond value being a 64-bit signed integer
Pure computation; no side effects

functions.name: PerfettoPbZigZagDecode32
functions.signature: static inline int32_t PerfettoPbZigZagDecode32(uint32_t value)
functions.description: Inverse of ZigZag encoding for 32-bit values; decodes an unsigned ZigZag-encoded value back to a signed 32-bit integer.
requirements: Input must be a value produced by ZigZag encoding (or any uint32_t is mathematically handled)
Pure computation; no side effects

functions.name: PerfettoPbZigZagDecode64
functions.signature: static inline int64_t PerfettoPbZigZagDecode64(uint64_t value)
functions.description: Inverse of ZigZag encoding for 64-bit values; decodes an unsigned ZigZag-encoded value back to a signed 64-bit integer.
requirements: Input should be a value produced by ZigZag encoding (or any uint64_t is mathematically handled)
Pure computation; no side effects

functions.name: PerfettoPbDoubleToFixed64
functions.signature: static inline uint64_t PerfettoPbDoubleToFixed64(double value)
functions.description: Bit-casts a double to the corresponding 64-bit fixed representation using memcpy, suitable for writing with PerfettoPbWriteFixed64 when serializing doubles.
requirements: No alignment or aliasing requirements for the caller; value is passed by value and bit-cast via memcpy
Result is the raw IEEE-754 bit pattern of the input double

functions.name: PerfettoPbFloatToFixed32
functions.signature: static inline uint32_t PerfettoPbFloatToFixed32(float value)
functions.description: Bit-casts a float to the corresponding 32-bit fixed representation using memcpy, suitable for writing with PerfettoPbWriteFixed32 when serializing floats.
requirements: No alignment or aliasing requirements for the caller; value is passed by value and bit-cast via memcpy
Result is the raw IEEE-754 bit pattern of the input float

functions.name: PerfettoPbPackedMsgUint64Append
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbPackedMsgUint64Append(struct PerfettoPbPackedMsgUint64* buf, uint64_t value)
functions.description: Append a uint64 value to a packed repeated field being serialized. Writes the value using protobuf varint encoding into the nested packed message buffer (buf->msg). Intended to be used between the corresponding PROTO_begin_* and PROTO_end_* calls of a packed repeated uint64 field.
requirements: buf must be a non-null pointer.
buf->msg must correspond to an active (begun) packed repeated uint64 field on a parent PerfettoPbMsg; call the appropriate PROTO_begin_* before the first append and PROTO_end_* after the last append.
May be called multiple times to append multiple elements to the same packed field.
value may be any 64-bit unsigned integer (0..2^64-1).
Do not call append after the packed field has been closed with PROTO_end_*.

functions.name: PerfettoPbPackedMsgUint32Append
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbPackedMsgUint32Append(struct PerfettoPbPackedMsgUint32* buf, uint32_t value)
functions.description: Append a uint32 value to a packed repeated field using protobuf varint encoding. Used within an in-progress packed repeated uint32 field.
requirements: buf must be a non-null pointer.
buf->msg must be initialized by beginning a packed repeated uint32 field on a parent message (via the corresponding PROTO_begin_*).
May be called multiple times to add elements.
value may be any 32-bit unsigned integer (0..2^32-1).
Must not be called after the packed field has been ended (PROTO_end_*).

functions.name: PerfettoPbPackedMsgInt64Append
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbPackedMsgInt64Append(struct PerfettoPbPackedMsgInt64* buf, int64_t value)
functions.description: Append an int64 value to a packed repeated field. The value is cast to uint64 and written using protobuf varint encoding (two’s complement representation).
requirements: buf must be a non-null pointer.
buf->msg must point to an active packed repeated int64 field begun on a parent message.
May be called multiple times to append elements.
value may be any 64-bit signed integer (−2^63..2^63−1).
Do not call after the packed field has been closed.

functions.name: PerfettoPbPackedMsgInt32Append
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbPackedMsgInt32Append(struct PerfettoPbPackedMsgInt32* buf, int32_t value)
functions.description: Append an int32 value to a packed repeated field. The value is cast to uint64 and written using protobuf varint encoding (two’s complement representation).
requirements: buf must be a non-null pointer.
buf->msg must be associated with an active packed repeated int32 field (opened with the appropriate PROTO_begin_*).
May be called repeatedly to append elements.
value may be any 32-bit signed integer (−2^31..2^31−1).
Do not append after the packed field has been ended.

functions.name: PerfettoPbPackedMsgSint64Append
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbPackedMsgSint64Append(struct PerfettoPbPackedMsgSint64* buf, int64_t value)
functions.description: Append a sint64 value (protobuf signed varint with zigzag) to a packed repeated field. Internally zigzag-encodes the signed value, then writes via varint encoding.
requirements: buf must be a non-null pointer.
buf->msg must be an active packed repeated sint64 field started on a parent message.
May be called multiple times to append values.
value may be any 64-bit signed integer (−2^63..2^63−1).
Must not be called after the packed field has been closed.

functions.name: PerfettoPbPackedMsgSint32Append
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbPackedMsgSint32Append(struct PerfettoPbPackedMsgSint32* buf, int32_t value)
functions.description: Append a sint32 value (protobuf signed varint with zigzag) to a packed repeated field. Performs zigzag encoding and writes the varint.
requirements: buf must be a non-null pointer.
buf->msg must correspond to an active packed repeated sint32 field on a parent message.
May be called repeatedly to append elements.
value may be any 32-bit signed integer (−2^31..2^31−1).
Do not call after the packed field has been ended.

functions.name: PerfettoPbPackedMsgFixed64Append
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbPackedMsgFixed64Append(struct PerfettoPbPackedMsgFixed64* buf, uint64_t value)
functions.description: Append a fixed64 value to a packed repeated field. Writes the 64-bit value in fixed-width (little-endian) protobuf encoding.
requirements: buf must be a non-null pointer.
buf->msg must be an active packed repeated fixed64 field on a parent message (begun via the corresponding PROTO_begin_*).
May be called multiple times to append elements.
value may be any 64-bit unsigned integer (0..2^64-1).
Must not append after the field has been ended.

functions.name: PerfettoPbPackedMsgFixed32Append
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbPackedMsgFixed32Append(struct PerfettoPbPackedMsgFixed32* buf, uint32_t value)
functions.description: Append a fixed32 value to a packed repeated field. Writes the 32-bit value in fixed-width (little-endian) protobuf encoding.
requirements: buf must be a non-null pointer.

functions.name: PerfettoPbPackedMsgSfixed64Append
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbPackedMsgSfixed64Append(struct PerfettoPbPackedMsgSfixed64* buf, int64_t value)
functions.description: Append an sfixed64 value to a packed repeated field. The signed 64-bit value is bitwise-copied and written using protobuf fixed64 encoding.
requirements: buf must be a non-null pointer.
buf->msg must be an active packed repeated sfixed64 field on a parent message.
May be called multiple times to append values.
value may be any 64-bit signed integer (−2^63..2^63−1).

functions.name: PerfettoPbPackedMsgSfixed32Append
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbPackedMsgSfixed32Append(struct PerfettoPbPackedMsgSfixed32* buf, int32_t value)
functions.description: Append an sfixed32 value to a packed repeated field. The signed 32-bit value is bitwise-copied and written using protobuf fixed32 encoding.
requirements: buf must be a non-null pointer.

functions.name: PerfettoPbPackedMsgDoubleAppend
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbPackedMsgDoubleAppend(struct PerfettoPbPackedMsgDouble* buf, double value)
functions.description: Append a double value to a packed repeated field. The IEEE-754 double is bitwise-copied and written using protobuf fixed64 encoding.
requirements: buf must be a non-null pointer.
buf->msg must be an active packed repeated double field on a parent message.
May be called multiple times to append values.
value may be any finite or non-finite double; it is written as raw bits without transformation.

functions.name: PerfettoPbPackedMsgFloatAppend
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbPackedMsgFloatAppend(struct PerfettoPbPackedMsgFloat* buf, float value)
functions.description: Append a float value to a packed repeated field. The IEEE-754 float is bitwise-copied and written using protobuf fixed32 encoding.
requirements: buf must be a non-null pointer.
buf->msg must correspond to an active packed repeated float field on a parent message.
May be called multiple times to append values.
value may be any finite or non-finite float; it is written as raw bits without transformation.
Must not append after the packed field has been ended.

functions.name: PerfettoPbMsgInit
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbMsgInit(struct PerfettoPbMsg* msg, struct PerfettoPbMsgWriter* writer)
functions.description: Initializes a PerfettoPbMsg to start writing a protobuf message using the provided PerfettoPbMsgWriter. Sets size to 0, clears size_field and parent/nested links. Typical usage: call once on a zeroed or fresh struct before appending fields.
requirements: msg must be a valid, writable pointer.
writer must be a valid, initialized PerfettoPbMsgWriter whose embedded PerfettoStreamWriter is ready for writes.
Must be called before any other PerfettoPbMsg* operations on msg.

functions.name: PerfettoPbMsgPatch
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbMsgPatch(struct PerfettoPbMsg* msg)
functions.description: Updates/patches the reserved size field location (if any) to a new address via the underlying stream writer, to keep the pending size varint pointer valid after the writer changes its backing buffer/range. Intended for internal use when stream writer ranges rotate.
requirements: msg must be initialized and have a valid msg->writer.
Safe to call regardless of msg->size_field being set; function uses the stream writer to re-annotate.

functions.name: PerfettoPbMsgPatchStack
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbMsgPatchStack(struct PerfettoPbMsg* msg)
functions.description: Walks up the parent chain and patches any pending size_field pointers that lie within the current stream writer memory range. Used to maintain correct patch locations for the current writer buffer for this message and its ancestors.
requirements: msg must be initialized with a valid writer.
Parent pointers (msg->parent chain) must either be NULL or point to valid PerfettoPbMsg instances sharing the same writer.

functions.name: PerfettoPbMsgAppendBytes
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbMsgAppendBytes(struct PerfettoPbMsg* msg, const uint8_t* begin, size_t size)
functions.description: Appends raw bytes to the message payload and increments msg->size accordingly. If the requested size exceeds currently available buffer space, it patches the stack to ensure size_field pointers remain valid, then writes.
requirements: msg must be initialized with a valid writer.
begin must point to at least size readable bytes.
The underlying writer must be capable of appending size bytes; if not, its reserve/append mechanisms must handle growth (handled internally).

functions.name: PerfettoPbMsgAppendByte
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbMsgAppendByte(struct PerfettoPbMsg* msg, uint8_t value)
functions.description: Convenience wrapper to append a single byte to the message payload.
requirements: msg must be initialized with a valid writer.

functions.name: PerfettoPbMsgAppendVarInt
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbMsgAppendVarInt(struct PerfettoPbMsg* msg, uint64_t value)
functions.description: Encodes value as a protobuf varint and appends it to the message payload.
requirements: msg must be initialized with a valid writer.

functions.name: PerfettoPbMsgAppendFixed64
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbMsgAppendFixed64(struct PerfettoPbMsg* msg, uint64_t value)
functions.description: Encodes value as a protobuf fixed64 (little-endian 8 bytes) and appends it to the payload.
requirements: msg must be initialized with a valid writer.

functions.name: PerfettoPbMsgAppendFixed32
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbMsgAppendFixed32(struct PerfettoPbMsg* msg, uint32_t value)
functions.description: Encodes value as a protobuf fixed32 (little-endian 4 bytes) and appends it to the payload.
requirements: msg must be initialized with a valid writer.

functions.name: PerfettoPbMsgAppendType0Field
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbMsgAppendType0Field(struct PerfettoPbMsg* msg, int32_t field_id, uint64_t value)
functions.description: Appends a field with wire type varint (type 0). Writes the tag for field_id and the varint-encoded value.
requirements: msg must be initialized with a valid writer.
field_id should be a valid protobuf field number (non-negative integer).
value is encoded as a protobuf varint.

functions.name: PerfettoPbMsgAppendType2Field
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbMsgAppendType2Field(struct PerfettoPbMsg* msg, int32_t field_id, const uint8_t* data, size_t size)
functions.description: Appends a length-delimited field (wire type 2). Writes the tag for field_id, the length varint, then size bytes from data.
requirements: msg must be initialized with a valid writer.
data must point to at least size readable bytes (size may be 0).
field_id should be a valid protobuf field number (non-negative integer).

functions.name: PerfettoPbMsgAppendFixed32Field
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbMsgAppendFixed32Field(struct PerfettoPbMsg* msg, int32_t field_id, uint32_t value)
functions.description: Appends a fixed32 field (wire type 5). Writes the tag for field_id and the 4-byte little-endian value.
requirements: msg must be initialized with a valid writer.
field_id should be a valid protobuf field number (non-negative integer).

functions.name: PerfettoPbMsgAppendFloatField
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbMsgAppendFloatField(struct PerfettoPbMsg* msg, int32_t field_id, float value)
functions.description: Appends a float field by reinterpreting the float bits and delegating to PerfettoPbMsgAppendFixed32Field (wire type 5).
requirements: msg must be initialized with a valid writer.
field_id should be a valid protobuf field number (non-negative integer).

functions.name: PerfettoPbMsgAppendFixed64Field
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbMsgAppendFixed64Field(struct PerfettoPbMsg* msg, int32_t field_id, uint64_t value)
functions.description: Appends a fixed64 field (wire type 1). Writes the tag for field_id and the 8-byte little-endian value.
requirements: msg must be initialized with a valid writer.
field_id should be a valid protobuf field number (non-negative integer).

functions.name: PerfettoPbMsgAppendDoubleField
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbMsgAppendDoubleField(struct PerfettoPbMsg* msg, int32_t field_id, double value)
functions.description: Appends a double field by reinterpreting the double bits and delegating to PerfettoPbMsgAppendFixed64Field (wire type 1).
requirements: msg must be initialized with a valid writer.
field_id should be a valid protobuf field number (non-negative integer).

functions.name: PerfettoPbMsgAppendCStrField
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbMsgAppendCStrField(struct PerfettoPbMsg* msg, int32_t field_id, const char* c_str)
functions.description: Appends a length-delimited string field from a NUL-terminated C string. Uses strlen(c_str) and writes the tag, length, and bytes.
requirements: msg must be initialized with a valid writer.
c_str must be a non-null, NUL-terminated string.
field_id should be a valid protobuf field number (non-negative integer).

functions.name: PerfettoPbMsgBeginNested
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbMsgBeginNested(struct PerfettoPbMsg* parent, struct PerfettoPbMsg* nested, int32_t field_id)
functions.description: Begins a nested (length-delimited) submessage within parent. Writes the tag on the parent, reserves a fixed-size patch area for the eventual length, initializes nested to write into the same writer, and links parent/nested relationships.
requirements: parent must be initialized with a valid writer.
nested must be a valid, writable pointer and will be initialized by this function (do not assume prior state).
field_id should be a valid protobuf field number (non-negative integer).
After finishing writing fields into nested, either call PerfettoPbMsgEndNested(parent) or call PerfettoPbMsgFinalize(parent) (which will end the nested message automatically).

functions.name: PerfettoPbMsgFinalize
functions.signature: static inline size_t PerfettoPbMsgFinalize(struct PerfettoPbMsg* msg)
functions.description: Finalizes a message: if a nested child is open, ends it; if a size_field was reserved (for a nested message), writes the length using a fixed-size, leading-zero varint encoding into that reserved area; clears size_field and returns the final payload size accumulated in msg->size. Typically called on the root message after all fields are appended, and on nested messages via PerfettoPbMsgEndNested.
requirements: msg must be initialized; if msg has an open nested child started via PerfettoPbMsgBeginNested, it will be ended automatically.
After finalization, the reserved size_field (if any) is consumed and cleared; do not rely on it further.
The returned size is the number of bytes appended so far; callers may use it to update parent sizes if managing manually.

functions.name: PerfettoPbMsgEndNested
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbMsgEndNested(struct PerfettoPbMsg* parent)
functions.description: Ends the current nested submessage started on parent with PerfettoPbMsgBeginNested by finalizing the nested message, adding its encoded size to the parent size, and clearing the parent->nested link.
requirements: parent must have an active nested child previously started with PerfettoPbMsgBeginNested.
parent must be initialized with a valid writer.

functions.name: PerfettoPbDecoderIterateBegin
functions.signature: static inline struct PerfettoPbDecoderIterator PerfettoPbDecoderIterateBegin(const void* start, size_t size)
functions.description: Initializes a protobuf decoding iterator over a top-level message buffer. It sets the internal decoder's read and end pointers to the provided byte range and parses the first field so iteration can begin immediately. Typical usage: call this to obtain an iterator, then loop while it.field.status == PERFETTO_PB_DECODER_OK and advance with PerfettoPbDecoderIterateNext.
requirements: start must point to a readable memory buffer of at least size bytes.
size must be the exact length (in bytes) of the protobuf message segment to parse.
Caller should begin iterating fields only if the initial it.field.status indicates success (PERFETTO_PB_DECODER_OK).
The iterator’s content becomes invalid if the underlying buffer is modified or freed during iteration.

functions.name: PerfettoPbDecoderIterateNestedBegin
functions.signature: static inline struct PerfettoPbDecoderIterator PerfettoPbDecoderIterateNestedBegin(struct PerfettoPbDecoderDelimitedField val)
functions.description: Initializes a protobuf decoding iterator for a nested (length-delimited) field. It treats the delimited field’s start pointer and length as a submessage and parses the first nested field for immediate iteration.
requirements: val.start must point to a readable memory region of at least val.len bytes.
val.len must be the exact length (in bytes) of the nested message payload.
Caller should begin iterating fields only if the initial it.field.status indicates success (PERFETTO_PB_DECODER_OK).
The iterator’s content becomes invalid if the underlying nested buffer is modified or freed during iteration.

functions.name: PerfettoPbDecoderIterateNext
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoPbDecoderIterateNext(struct PerfettoPbDecoderIterator* iterator)
functions.description: Advances the protobuf decoding iterator to the next field within the current message range by parsing from the iterator’s internal read pointer. After calling, the iterator->field reflects the next parsed field or an error/end state.
requirements: iterator must be non-null.
iterator must have been initialized by PerfettoPbDecoderIterateBegin or PerfettoPbDecoderIterateNestedBegin (i.e., must contain a valid decoder state).
Caller should check iterator->field.status after the call to determine success or end-of-message before accessing field contents.
The underlying message buffer must remain valid for the lifetime of iteration.

functions.name: PerfettoPbDecoderFieldGetUint32
functions.signature: static inline bool PerfettoPbDecoderFieldGetUint32(const PerfettoPbDecoderField* field, uint32_t* out)
functions.description: Attempts to extract the current field’s value as a 32-bit unsigned integer. Supports VARINT, FIXED64, and FIXED32 wire types; performs narrowing when necessary. Returns true on successful extraction and writes the result to out; otherwise returns false.
requirements: field must be non-null and refer to a parsed field.
out must be non-null.
For success, field->wire_type must be one of PERFETTO_PB_WIRE_TYPE_VARINT, PERFETTO_PB_WIRE_TYPE_FIXED64, or PERFETTO_PB_WIRE_TYPE_FIXED32; otherwise the function returns false.
Caller must check the boolean return value before using *out.
When sourced from 64-bit storage, the value is cast to uint32_t and may truncate; caller should ensure the value fits if truncation is undesirable.

functions.name: PerfettoPbDecoderFieldGetInt32
functions.signature: static inline bool PerfettoPbDecoderFieldGetInt32(const PerfettoPbDecoderField* field, int32_t* out)
functions.description: Attempts to extract the current field’s value as a 32-bit signed integer. Supports VARINT, FIXED64, and FIXED32 wire types; performs narrowing when necessary. Returns true on success and writes to out; otherwise returns false.
requirements: field must be non-null and refer to a parsed field.
out must be non-null.
For success, field->wire_type must be one of PERFETTO_PB_WIRE_TYPE_VARINT, PERFETTO_PB_WIRE_TYPE_FIXED64, or PERFETTO_PB_WIRE_TYPE_FIXED32; otherwise the function returns false.
Caller must check the boolean return value before using *out.
When sourced from 64-bit storage, the value is cast to int32_t and may truncate; caller should ensure the value fits if truncation is undesirable.

functions.name: PerfettoPbDecoderFieldGetUint64
functions.signature: static inline bool PerfettoPbDecoderFieldGetUint64(const PerfettoPbDecoderField* field, uint64_t* out)
functions.description: Attempts to extract the current field’s value as a 64-bit unsigned integer. Supports VARINT, FIXED64, and FIXED32 wire types. Returns true on success and writes to out; otherwise returns false.
requirements: field must be non-null and refer to a parsed field.
out must be non-null.
For success, field->wire_type must be one of PERFETTO_PB_WIRE_TYPE_VARINT, PERFETTO_PB_WIRE_TYPE_FIXED64, or PERFETTO_PB_WIRE_TYPE_FIXED32; otherwise the function returns false.
Caller must check the boolean return value before using *out.
When sourced from FIXED32, the 32-bit value is zero-extended to 64 bits.

functions.name: PerfettoPbDecoderFieldGetInt64
functions.signature: static inline bool PerfettoPbDecoderFieldGetInt64(const PerfettoPbDecoderField* field, int64_t* out)
functions.description: Attempts to extract the current field’s value as a 64-bit signed integer. Supports VARINT, FIXED64, and FIXED32 wire types. Returns true on success and writes to out; otherwise returns false.
requirements: field must be non-null and refer to a parsed field.
out must be non-null.
For success, field->wire_type must be one of PERFETTO_PB_WIRE_TYPE_VARINT, PERFETTO_PB_WIRE_TYPE_FIXED64, or PERFETTO_PB_WIRE_TYPE_FIXED32; otherwise the function returns false.
Caller must check the boolean return value before using *out.
When sourced from FIXED32, the 32-bit value is cast to int64_t (sign is preserved only for FIXED32 signed interpretation per cast semantics).

functions.name: PerfettoPbDecoderFieldGetBool
functions.signature: static inline bool PerfettoPbDecoderFieldGetBool(const PerfettoPbDecoderField* field, bool* out)
functions.description: Attempts to extract the current field’s value as a boolean. Supports VARINT, FIXED64, and FIXED32 wire types. Nonzero values convert to true, zero to false. Returns true on success and writes to out; otherwise returns false.
requirements: field must be non-null and refer to a parsed field.
out must be non-null.
For success, field->wire_type must be one of PERFETTO_PB_WIRE_TYPE_VARINT, PERFETTO_PB_WIRE_TYPE_FIXED64, or PERFETTO_PB_WIRE_TYPE_FIXED32; otherwise the function returns false.
Caller must check the boolean return value before using *out.

functions.name: PerfettoPbDecoderFieldGetFloat
functions.signature: static inline bool PerfettoPbDecoderFieldGetFloat(const PerfettoPbDecoderField* field, float* out)
functions.description: Attempts to extract the current field’s value as a 32-bit floating-point number. Supports FIXED64 (converted from double) and FIXED32 (native float) wire types. Returns true on success and writes to out; otherwise returns false.
requirements: field must be non-null and refer to a parsed field.
out must be non-null.
For success, field->wire_type must be PERFETTO_PB_WIRE_TYPE_FIXED64 or PERFETTO_PB_WIRE_TYPE_FIXED32; otherwise the function returns false.
Caller must check the boolean return value before using *out.
Converting from double (FIXED64) to float may lose precision; caller should account for this if precision matters.

functions.name: PerfettoPbDecoderFieldGetDouble
functions.signature: static inline bool PerfettoPbDecoderFieldGetDouble(const PerfettoPbDecoderField* field, double* out)
functions.description: Attempts to extract the current field’s value as a 64-bit floating-point number. Supports FIXED64 (native double) and FIXED32 (promoted from float) wire types. Returns true on success and writes to out; otherwise returns false.
requirements: field must be non-null and refer to a parsed field.
out must be non-null.
For success, field->wire_type must be PERFETTO_PB_WIRE_TYPE_FIXED64 or PERFETTO_PB_WIRE_TYPE_FIXED32; otherwise the function returns false.
Caller must check the boolean return value before using *out.

functions.name: PerfettoStreamWriterAvailableBytes
functions.signature: static inline size_t PerfettoStreamWriterAvailableBytes(const struct PerfettoStreamWriter* w)
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes currently available for writing in the active chunk of the PerfettoStreamWriter. Intended to be used to check capacity before writing or reserving space.
requirements: w must be non-null.
w must point to a properly initialized PerfettoStreamWriter with valid begin, write_ptr, and end pointers.
w->end must be at or after w->write_ptr (no underflow/overflow).

functions.name: PerfettoStreamWriterAppendBytesUnsafe
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoStreamWriterAppendBytesUnsafe(struct PerfettoStreamWriter* w, const uint8_t* src, size_t size)
functions.description: Copies size bytes from src into the writer at the current write position and advances the write pointer. This variant assumes sufficient space is already available and performs no growth or bounds handling.
requirements: w must be non-null and properly initialized.
PerfettoStreamWriterAvailableBytes(w) must be >= size (explicit requirement; function asserts this).
src must point to at least size readable bytes; if size is 0, src may be null.
Destination and src regions must not overlap (memcpy has undefined behavior on overlap).

functions.name: PerfettoStreamWriterAppendBytes
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoStreamWriterAppendBytes(struct PerfettoStreamWriter* w, const uint8_t* src, size_t size)
functions.description: Appends size bytes from src to the writer, growing to a new chunk via PerfettoStreamWriterAppendBytesSlowpath if the current chunk lacks space. Advances the write pointer by size.
requirements: w must be non-null and properly initialized with a delegate capable of supplying new chunks on demand.
src must point to at least size readable bytes; if size is 0, src may be null.
If size <= available bytes, behavior is identical to the unsafe variant (no overlap between src and destination; memcpy requires non-overlapping regions).
If size exceeds current capacity, the underlying slowpath must succeed in providing space; otherwise behavior is unspecified by this header.

functions.name: PerfettoStreamWriterAppendByte
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoStreamWriterAppendByte(struct PerfettoStreamWriter* w, uint8_t value)
functions.description: Writes a single byte to the writer, allocating a new chunk via PerfettoStreamWriterNewChunk if the current chunk has no remaining space. Advances the write pointer by 1.
requirements: w must be non-null and properly initialized with a delegate capable of supplying new chunks on demand.
No other explicit constraints; if the current chunk is full, the function will request a new chunk internally.

functions.name: PerfettoStreamWriterReserveBytesUnsafe
functions.signature: static inline uint8_t* PerfettoStreamWriterReserveBytesUnsafe(struct PerfettoStreamWriter* w, size_t size)
functions.description: Reserves size bytes in the current chunk and returns a pointer to the reserved area. The reserved region is considered written and will not be reused by the writer. The caller can write directly into the returned buffer.
requirements: w must be non-null and properly initialized.
PerfettoStreamWriterAvailableBytes(w) must be >= size (explicit requirement; function asserts this).
Caller must not exceed the reserved size when writing to the returned buffer.
The returned pointer becomes invalid if the writer switches chunks later; use it immediately or before further writes that may cause a chunk change.

functions.name: PerfettoStreamWriterReserveBytes
functions.signature: static inline uint8_t* PerfettoStreamWriterReserveBytes(struct PerfettoStreamWriter* w, size_t size)
functions.description: Reserves size bytes for direct writing and returns a pointer to that region, growing via PerfettoStreamWriterReserveBytesSlowpath if necessary. The reserved area is considered written by the writer and will not be reused.
requirements: w must be non-null and properly initialized with a delegate capable of supplying new chunks on demand.
WARNING in header: size should be smaller than the chunk size returned by the delegate.
Caller must not exceed the reserved size when writing to the returned buffer.
The returned pointer is valid for the reserved region at the time of return; further writes that cause a chunk switch may invalidate previously returned pointers.

functions.name: PerfettoStreamWriterGetWrittenSize
functions.signature: static inline size_t PerfettoStreamWriterGetWrittenSize(const struct PerfettoStreamWriter* w)
functions.description: Returns the total number of bytes written to the stream from the start, including previous chunks and the current write position.
requirements: w must be non-null and properly initialized.
w->written_previously must reflect the bytes written in prior chunks and be maintained by the writer implementation; begin and write_ptr must be valid for the current chunk.

functions.name: PerfettoTracingSessionCreate
functions.signature: static inline struct PerfettoTracingSessionImpl* PerfettoTracingSessionCreate(PerfettoBackendTypes backend)
functions.description: Factory function that creates a Perfetto tracing session for the requested backend. If backend is PERFETTO_BACKEND_IN_PROCESS it returns a session created by PerfettoTracingSessionInProcessCreate(); if backend is PERFETTO_BACKEND_SYSTEM it returns a session created by PerfettoTracingSessionSystemCreate(); otherwise it returns nullptr. Typical usage: select a backend constant, call this function, and check the returned pointer before use. Notes: the exact lifetime management (how to destroy the session) is not documented here; consult the corresponding ABI for destruction/release APIs. Returns nullptr for unsupported or unrecognized backends.
requirements: The backend argument should be a valid PerfettoBackendTypes value; to obtain a non-null session, pass PERFETTO_BACKEND_IN_PROCESS or PERFETTO_BACKEND_SYSTEM.
The caller must check the return value for nullptr before dereferencing or using the session pointer.

The returned pointer refers to an implementation-defined PerfettoTracingSessionImpl; callers should use only the public/ABI APIs intended to operate on this type (exact destruction/cleanup API not specified here).

functions.name: PerfettoProducerInit
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoProducerInit(struct PerfettoProducerInitArgs args)
functions.description: Initializes the global Perfetto producer backends according to the provided arguments. May be called multiple times; if a backend is already initialized, most fields in args are ignored. Typical usage: construct a PerfettoProducerInitArgs (e.g., with PERFETTO_PRODUCER_INIT_ARGS_INIT()), set the desired backends bitmask and optional shared memory size hint, then call this function once early in process startup.
requirements: args.backends is a bitwise-OR of PerfettoBackendTypes and selects which backends to initialize.
args.shmem_size_hint_kb, if set, must be a multiple of 4 KB; values larger than kMaxShmSize (32 MB) or not 4 KB-aligned may be ignored by the implementation.
Function is safe to call multiple times; re-initialization attempts may ignore most of args for already-initialized backends.
Callers should ensure struct PerfettoProducerInitArgs is initialized (e.g., PERFETTO_PRODUCER_INIT_ARGS_INIT()) before use.

functions.name: PerfettoProducerActivateTrigger
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoProducerActivateTrigger(const char* trigger_name, uint32_t ttl_ms)
functions.description: Requests activation of a single trigger in tracing services. Sends the trigger to all initialized backends that are currently connected and those that connect within ttl_ms milliseconds. Returns immediately without waiting for delivery. Intended to unblock tracing sessions waiting on the named trigger.
requirements: trigger_name should be a valid, null-terminated C string naming the trigger to activate.
ttl_ms is a time-to-live in milliseconds; backends connecting within this window should receive the trigger.
Function can be called after at least one backend has been initialized; triggers are sent only to initialized/connected backends.

functions.name: PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgsCreate
functions.signature: struct PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgs* PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgsCreate(void);
functions.description: Allocates and returns an opaque PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgs object used to configure backend initialization (e.g., shared memory size hint). Intended to be paired with PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgsDestroy after use.
requirements: Must be paired with PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgsDestroy to avoid resource leaks.
Return value must be checked for null if the underlying implementation can fail (unknown from this header).
The returned object is intended to be passed to backend init functions such as PerfettoProducerInProcessInit and/or PerfettoProducerSystemInit before destruction.

functions.name: PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgsSetShmemSizeHintKb
functions.signature: void PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgsSetShmemSizeHintKb(struct PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgs* args, uint32_t shmem_size_hint_kb);
functions.description: Sets a shared memory buffer size hint (in kilobytes) on a PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgs object. Backends may use this to size the shared memory buffer used for trace data. Values may be ignored if unsupported.
requirements: args must be a valid pointer previously returned by PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgsCreate and not yet destroyed.
shmem_size_hint_kb is expressed in kilobytes.
shmem_size_hint_kb should be a multiple of 4 KB (i.e., a multiple of 4 in KB units); values not meeting this may be ignored (per comments in this header).
Very large values (greater than the backend’s maximum, e.g., 32 MB mentioned in comments) may be ignored.
Must be called before initializing a backend with PerfettoProducerInProcessInit/PerfettoProducerSystemInit for the hint to take effect.

functions.name: PerfettoProducerInProcessInit
functions.signature: void PerfettoProducerInProcessInit(struct PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgs* args);
functions.description: Initializes the in-process Perfetto producer backend using the provided initialization arguments. Safe to call multiple times; subsequent calls may ignore most arguments if already initialized (as implied by the higher-level wrapper).
requirements: args must be a valid pointer created by PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgsCreate and not yet destroyed at the time of the call.
Can be called multiple times; if the backend is already initialized, arguments may be ignored (behavior inferred from wrapper comments).
Should be called before producing/activating triggers intended for the in-process backend to have effect.

functions.name: PerfettoProducerSystemInit
functions.signature: void PerfettoProducerSystemInit(struct PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgs* args);
functions.description: Initializes the system Perfetto producer backend using the provided initialization arguments. Safe to call multiple times; subsequent calls may ignore most arguments if already initialized (as implied by the higher-level wrapper).
requirements: args must be a valid pointer created by PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgsCreate and not yet destroyed at the time of the call.
Can be called multiple times; if the backend is already initialized, arguments may be ignored (behavior inferred from wrapper comments).
Should be called before producing/activating triggers intended for the system backend to have effect.

functions.name: PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgsDestroy
functions.signature: void PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgsDestroy(struct PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgs* args);
functions.description: Destroys and releases resources associated with a PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgs object created by PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgsCreate.
requirements: args must be a pointer previously returned by PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgsCreate.
args must not be used after this function returns (dangling pointer).
Should be called exactly once per successfully created args object to avoid leaks; safe handling of null is unknown from this header.
Should be called after all desired backend initializations have been performed with the args object.

functions.name: PerfettoProducerActivateTriggers
functions.signature: void PerfettoProducerActivateTriggers(const char* const trigger_names[], uint32_t ttl_ms);
functions.description: Requests activation of one or more trigger names across all initialized backends. Each backend that is currently connected—and any that connect within ttl_ms milliseconds—will receive the trigger activation request. Returns immediately.
requirements: trigger_names must be a null-terminated array of C string pointers (the last element must be null/PERFETTO_NULL).
Each non-null entry in trigger_names must point to a valid, null-terminated C string that remains valid for the duration of the call.
ttl_ms specifies a time window in milliseconds as an unsigned 32-bit value; a value of 0 applies only to currently connected backends.
For triggers to have any effect, at least one backend should be initialized (in-process and/or system).
The array itself must be readable up to and including the terminating null entry.

functions.name: PerfettoTeRegisterCategories
functions.signature: void PerfettoTeRegisterCategories(struct PerfettoTeCategory** categories, size_t count);
functions.description: Registers an array of Perfetto track event categories with the tracing service. Intended to be called after defining categories and before they are used for tracing. Typically followed by a publish step to make the registration visible to the service.
requirements: categories must point to the first element of an array of pointers to valid, initialized PerfettoTeCategory objects.
count must be the number of elements in the categories array.
The provided PerfettoTeCategory objects must remain alive and unmodified while registered.
This function is inferred to return void; callers should not expect a return value or error code.

functions.name: PerfettoTePublishCategories
functions.signature: void PerfettoTePublishCategories(void);
functions.description: Publishes the current category registry state to the tracing service so that newly registered or unregistered categories become visible. Used after registering or unregistering categories.
requirements: Should be called after PerfettoTeRegisterCategories or PerfettoTeUnregisterCategories to apply changes.
This function is inferred to return void; callers should not expect a return value or error code.

functions.name: PerfettoTeUnregisterCategories
functions.signature: void PerfettoTeUnregisterCategories(struct PerfettoTeCategory** categories, size_t count);
functions.description: Unregisters a set of previously registered categories from the tracing service. After unregistration, those categories must no longer be used for tracing.
requirements: categories must point to the first element of an array of pointers to previously registered PerfettoTeCategory objects.
count must be the number of elements in the categories array.
After unregistration, the categories cannot be used for tracing; executing PERFETTO_TE() on unregistered categories will cause a null pointer dereference (as warned in the header).
Should be followed by PerfettoTePublishCategories to apply changes.
This function is inferred to return void; callers should not expect a return value or error code.

functions.name: PerfettoPbZigZagEncode64
functions.signature: uint64_t PerfettoPbZigZagEncode64(int64_t value)
functions.description: Encodes a signed 64-bit integer using Protocol Buffers ZigZag encoding, producing an unsigned 64-bit varint-friendly representation. Used by PERFETTO_TE_PROTO_FIELD_ZIGZAG to populate sint* protobuf fields.
requirements: Input value must be representable as int64_t.
Returns an unsigned 64-bit ZigZag-encoded integer suitable for varint serialization.

functions.name: perfetto::internal::MakeTeCleanup
functions.signature: template <typename F> perfetto::internal::TeCleanup<F> MakeTeCleanup(F&& f)
functions.description: Factory that creates a TeCleanup<F> RAII object which invokes the provided callable f exactly once in its destructor. Intended for emitting a paired cleanup action at scope exit (e.g., to auto-emit PERFETTO_TE_SLICE_END()). Usage: store the returned object in a local variable (typically via auto) to ensure f runs when the variable leaves scope.
requirements: Template parameter F must be callable with no arguments (i.e., f() must be valid).
The callable is stored by value via perfect forwarding; if f holds references, referenced objects must outlive the TeCleanup instance.
The TeCleanup object is non-copyable and non-movable; keep it in a single scope-bound variable.
The cleanup callable will be invoked unconditionally in the TeCleanup destructor; ensure it is safe to call at that time.
Avoid returning a temporary from MakeTeCleanup without binding to a local, otherwise the destructor will run immediately.

functions.name: PerfettoDsParamsDefault
functions.signature: static inline struct PerfettoDsParams PerfettoDsParamsDefault(void)
functions.description: Returns a PerfettoDsParams struct initialized to library defaults. Use this to obtain a baseline set of data source parameters, then override any fields as needed before registration. Purpose: provide a safe, fully-initialized params object. Expected usage: call this, modify callbacks, policies, and flags, then pass the result to PerfettoDsRegister.
requirements: May be called at any time before PerfettoDsRegister.
Returned struct is a value; the caller may modify any fields before use.
No allocation or cleanup is required for the returned value.

functions.name: PerfettoDsRegister
functions.signature: static inline bool PerfettoDsRegister(struct PerfettoDs* ds, const char* data_source_name, struct PerfettoDsParams params)
functions.description: Registers a data source type with the global Perfetto producer under the given name and parameters. Purpose: initialize ds, build and send a DataSourceDescriptor, and wire up lifecycle and TLS/incremental-state callbacks. Expected usage: prepare a PerfettoDs (often PERFETTO_DS_INIT), prepare params (e.g., via PerfettoDsParamsDefault and set callbacks), then call this once during initialization. Returns true on success, false on failure.
requirements: ds must be a valid, writable pointer; the function initializes ds->enabled and ds->impl.
data_source_name must be a valid, NUL-terminated C string; it is serialized into the descriptor.
params may be obtained from PerfettoDsParamsDefault() and optionally customized; all callbacks are optional and may be NULL.
On success, ds->impl is set and ds->enabled will later reflect enablement state; callers must retain ds for the lifetime they intend to trace.
The function performs a heap allocation for the descriptor internally and frees it; the caller must not free anything returned by this function.
Must be called before attempting to iterate or trace with this data source.
If returns false, the data source was not registered; callers should not use ds->impl and may retry or handle the error.

functions.name: PerfettoDsTraceIterateBegin
functions.signature: static inline struct PerfettoDsTracerIterator PerfettoDsTraceIterateBegin(struct PerfettoDs* ds)
functions.description: Begins iteration over all active instances of the given data source type on the current thread. Purpose: acquire an iterator to traverse per-instance tracing contexts when emitting trace data. Expected usage: call this, check iterator.impl.tracer for NULL, then loop calling PerfettoDsTraceIterateNext until traversal completes (tracer becomes NULL), or call PerfettoDsTraceIterateBreak to end early.
requirements: ds must be a registered data source (PerfettoDsRegister succeeded).
Must be called on the thread where instance iteration is intended; iteration enumerates instances active on this thread.
If ds->enabled is false, the returned iterator will have impl.tracer == NULL and no iteration is needed.
If iteration will be terminated early, the caller must invoke PerfettoDsTraceIterateBreak before discarding the iterator.

functions.name: PerfettoDsTraceIterateNext
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoDsTraceIterateNext(struct PerfettoDs* ds, struct PerfettoDsTracerIterator* iterator)
functions.description: Advances the iterator to the next active instance of the data source on the current thread. Purpose: step through instances when emitting trace data. Expected usage: used in a loop after PerfettoDsTraceIterateBegin until iterator->impl.tracer becomes NULL.
requirements: ds must be the same data source used to start iteration.
iterator must have been initialized by PerfettoDsTraceIterateBegin and not yet broken with PerfettoDsTraceIterateBreak.
Must not be called after iterator->impl.tracer becomes NULL.

functions.name: PerfettoDsTraceIterateBreak
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoDsTraceIterateBreak(struct PerfettoDs* ds, struct PerfettoDsTracerIterator* iterator)
functions.description: Ends iteration early and releases any resources associated with the iterator. Purpose: provide a safe way to break out of an active-instances iteration before completion. Expected usage: call this instead of a raw loop break when terminating iteration early, then stop using the iterator.
requirements: ds must be the same data source used to start iteration.
iterator must currently refer to an active iteration (impl.tracer non-NULL) when breaking early; the function is a no-op if tracer is NULL.
After calling, the iterator must not be used further in that iteration context.

functions.name: PerfettoDsGetCustomTls
functions.signature: static inline void* PerfettoDsGetCustomTls(struct PerfettoDs* ds, struct PerfettoDsTracerIterator* iterator)
functions.description: Returns the per-instance custom thread-local state for the current iterator’s active instance. Purpose: access user-defined TLS created by the data source callbacks. Expected usage: call during a trace point while iterating instances to get a pointer previously created by the on_create_tls_cb callback (if provided).
requirements: ds must be a registered data source; iterator must be valid and currently refer to an active tracer instance.
Should be called from within an iteration context (between Begin and Next/End/Break calls) where iterator->impl.tracer is non-NULL.
If no TLS callback was set or no state exists, the returned pointer may be NULL; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: PerfettoDsGetIncrementalState
functions.signature: static inline void* PerfettoDsGetIncrementalState(struct PerfettoDs* ds, struct PerfettoDsTracerIterator* iterator)
functions.description: Returns the per-instance incremental state for the current iterator’s active instance. Purpose: access user-defined incremental state that may be reset by the tracing service. Expected usage: call during a trace point while iterating instances to get a pointer previously created by the on_create_incr_cb callback (if provided).
requirements: ds must be a registered data source; iterator must be valid and currently refer to an active tracer instance.
Should be called from within an iteration context where iterator->impl.tracer is non-NULL.
Incremental state may be cleared by the tracing service; callers must tolerate a NULL or reset state and reinitialize as needed.

functions.name: PerfettoDsTracerPacketBegin
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoDsTracerPacketBegin(struct PerfettoDsTracerIterator* iterator, struct PerfettoDsRootTracePacket* root)
functions.description: Begins writing a new TracePacket for the data source instance referenced by iterator and initializes root with a writer and TracePacket message. Purpose: open a packet to serialize fields into via the protobuf writer. Expected usage: call this during iteration, populate root->msg using generated encoders, then call PerfettoDsTracerPacketEnd to finalize and emit.
requirements: iterator must refer to a valid active tracer instance (iterator->impl.tracer non-NULL).
root must be a valid, writable pointer; its fields are initialized by this call and must not be assumed valid beforehand.
Each successful Begin must be paired with a corresponding PerfettoDsTracerPacketEnd using the same iterator and root before reusing root or ending iteration.
Do not use root->writer or root->msg before Begin or after End.

functions.name: PerfettoDsTracerPacketEnd
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoDsTracerPacketEnd(struct PerfettoDsTracerIterator* iterator, struct PerfettoDsRootTracePacket* root)
functions.description: Finalizes the TracePacket started with PerfettoDsTracerPacketBegin and commits it to the data source instance. Purpose: close the protobuf message and flush the packet to the tracing backend. Expected usage: call after finishing all field writes into root->msg.
requirements: Must be called only after a matching PerfettoDsTracerPacketBegin on the same iterator and root.
iterator must still refer to the same active tracer instance used for Begin.
After End returns, root’s writer/message must not be used unless reinitialized with a new Begin.

functions.name: PerfettoDsTracerFlush
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoDsTracerFlush(struct PerfettoDsTracerIterator* iterator, PerfettoDsTracerOnFlushCb cb, void* ctx)
functions.description: Requests a flush of the current data source instance’s buffers and registers a callback to be invoked upon flush completion. Purpose: coordinate flushing from within a trace point. Expected usage: call during iteration to schedule/perform a flush; cb will be called with the provided ctx when the flush completes.
requirements: iterator must refer to a valid active tracer instance (iterator->impl.tracer non-NULL).
cb may be NULL if no completion notification is needed; if non-NULL, it must conform to PerfettoDsTracerOnFlushCb.
The callback will be invoked by the tracing implementation; ctx is an opaque user pointer passed through unchanged.

functions.name: PerfettoTeCategoryRegister
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoTeCategoryRegister(struct PerfettoTeCategory* cat)
functions.description: Registers a category with the tracing backend by creating its implementation, retrieving its enabled flag pointer, and obtaining its interned-id (iid). Intended to be called after filling cat->desc and before emitting any events for this category.
requirements: cat must be a non-null pointer.
cat->desc must be fully initialized before calling (explicitly stated).
cat must not already be registered; calling again without unregistering may leak or corrupt internal state (inferred from creating a new impl without cleanup).

functions.name: PerfettoTeRegisterCategories
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoTeRegisterCategories(struct PerfettoTeCategory* cats[], size_t size)
functions.description: Registers multiple categories by calling PerfettoTeCategoryRegister on each entry of the array.
requirements: cats must be a non-null pointer to an array of size elements.
Each cats[i] must be a non-null pointer to a PerfettoTeCategory with desc initialized before the call (follows the single-register requirements).

functions.name: PerfettoTeCategorySetCallback
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoTeCategorySetCallback(struct PerfettoTeCategory* reg_cat, PerfettoTeCategoryImplCallback cb, void* user_arg)
functions.description: Registers a callback to be invoked when data source instances with the given category are created or destroyed. user_arg is passed through to the callback. Passing NULL for cb disables the callback.
requirements: reg_cat must be a non-null pointer to a previously registered category (uses reg_cat->impl).
cb may be NULL to disable the callback (explicit).
The callback must conform to PerfettoTeCategoryImplCallback signature (details defined in included ABI).

functions.name: PerfettoTeCategoryUnregister
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoTeCategoryUnregister(struct PerfettoTeCategory* cat)
functions.description: Unregisters a previously registered category, destroying its implementation and resetting its fields. After this call, the category must not be used for tracing.
requirements: cat must be a non-null pointer to a previously registered category.
After calling, do not use the category in tracing; doing so can cause a null pointer dereference (explicit warning).

functions.name: PerfettoTeUnregisterCategories
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoTeUnregisterCategories(struct PerfettoTeCategory* cats[], size_t size)
functions.description: Unregisters multiple categories by calling PerfettoTeCategoryUnregister on each entry of the array.
requirements: cats must be a non-null pointer to an array of size elements.
Each cats[i] must be a non-null pointer to a previously registered category.
After calling, none of the categories may be used for tracing; doing so can cause a null pointer dereference (explicit warning).

functions.name: PerfettoTeProcessTrackUuid
functions.signature: static inline uint64_t PerfettoTeProcessTrackUuid(void)
functions.description: Returns the UUID of the process track for the current process.

functions.name: PerfettoTeThreadTrackUuid
functions.signature: static inline uint64_t PerfettoTeThreadTrackUuid(void)
functions.description: Returns the UUID of the current thread's track, derived from the process track UUID and the current thread id.

functions.name: PerfettoTeGlobalTrackUuid
functions.signature: static inline uint64_t PerfettoTeGlobalTrackUuid(void)
functions.description: Returns the root/global track UUID (constant 0).

functions.name: PerfettoTeCounterTrackUuid
functions.signature: static inline uint64_t PerfettoTeCounterTrackUuid(const char* name, uint64_t parent_uuid)
functions.description: Computes a deterministic UUID for a counter track identified by its name and parent track UUID.
requirements: name must be a non-null, NUL-terminated C string (uses strlen).
parent_uuid can be any 64-bit value (0 to indicate no parent).

functions.name: PerfettoTeNamedTrackUuid
functions.signature: static inline uint64_t PerfettoTeNamedTrackUuid(const char* name, uint64_t id, uint64_t parent_uuid)
functions.description: Computes a deterministic UUID for a named track using its name, a unique id, and the parent track UUID.
requirements: name must be a non-null, NUL-terminated C string (uses strlen).
id should be unique for the given name/parent combination to avoid collisions (implied by purpose).
parent_uuid can be any 64-bit value (0 to indicate no parent).

functions.name: PerfettoTeCounterTrackFillDesc
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoTeCounterTrackFillDesc(struct perfetto_protos_TrackDescriptor* desc, const char* name, uint64_t parent_track_uuid, uint64_t track_uuid)
functions.description: Serializes fields into a TrackDescriptor proto for a counter track: sets uuid, optional parent_uuid, name, and marks it as a CounterDescriptor.
requirements: desc must point to a valid, initialized perfetto_protos_TrackDescriptor message (initialize via PerfettoPbMsgInit with an associated writer before calling).
name must be a non-null, NUL-terminated C string.
track_uuid must be the UUID computed for this counter track (as per comment, via PerfettoTeCounterTrackUuid).
parent_track_uuid may be 0 to omit the parent field.

functions.name: PerfettoTeNamedTrackFillDesc
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoTeNamedTrackFillDesc(struct perfetto_protos_TrackDescriptor* desc, const char* track_name, uint64_t id, uint64_t parent_track_uuid, uint64_t track_uuid)
functions.description: Serializes fields into a TrackDescriptor proto for a named track: sets uuid, optional parent_uuid, and name. The id parameter is unused in serialization here.
requirements: desc must point to a valid, initialized perfetto_protos_TrackDescriptor message (initialize via PerfettoPbMsgInit with an associated writer before calling).
track_name must be a non-null, NUL-terminated C string.
track_uuid must be the UUID computed for this named track (as per comment, via PerfettoTeNamedTrackUuid).
parent_track_uuid may be 0 to omit the parent field.

functions.name: PerfettoTeNamedTrackRegister
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoTeNamedTrackRegister(struct PerfettoTeRegisteredTrack* track, const char* name, uint64_t id, uint64_t parent_track_uuid)
functions.description: Builds and stores a serialized TrackDescriptor for a named track into track->impl by allocating a heap buffer, writing the descriptor, and copying it into a malloced buffer. Also stores the computed track UUID.
requirements: track must be a non-null pointer. It should not already hold an allocated descriptor to avoid leaking memory (function overwrites without freeing).
name must be a non-null, NUL-terminated C string.
id should uniquely identify the track with the given name/parent (per intended use).
Caller is responsible for later calling PerfettoTeRegisteredTrackUnregister to free allocated memory.

functions.name: PerfettoTeCounterTrackRegister
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoTeCounterTrackRegister(struct PerfettoTeRegisteredTrack* track, const char* name, uint64_t parent_track_uuid)
functions.description: Builds and stores a serialized TrackDescriptor for a counter track into track->impl by allocating a heap buffer, writing the descriptor, and copying it into a malloced buffer. Also stores the computed track UUID.
requirements: track must be a non-null pointer. It should not already hold an allocated descriptor to avoid leaking memory (function overwrites without freeing).
name must be a non-null, NUL-terminated C string.
Caller is responsible for later calling PerfettoTeRegisteredTrackUnregister to free allocated memory.

functions.name: PerfettoTeRegisteredTrackUnregister
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoTeRegisteredTrackUnregister(struct PerfettoTeRegisteredTrack* track)
functions.description: Unregisters a previously registered track by freeing its stored descriptor and resetting the descriptor pointer and size.
requirements: track must be a non-null pointer to a previously registered track or one with a possibly null descriptor pointer (free is safe with NULL).
After calling, track->impl.descriptor is set to NULL and size to 0; any previous references to the freed memory become invalid.

functions.name: PerfettoTeProcessScopedFlow
functions.signature: static inline struct PerfettoTeFlow PerfettoTeProcessScopedFlow(uint64_t id)
functions.description: Creates a flow identifier scoped to the current process by XORing the provided id with the process track UUID. Used to link events within the same process.
requirements: No special constraints on id; it is combined with the process UUID.

functions.name: PerfettoTeGlobalFlow
functions.signature: static inline struct PerfettoTeFlow PerfettoTeGlobalFlow(uint64_t id)
functions.description: Creates a global flow identifier equal to the provided id. Used to link events across processes.

functions.name: PerfettoTeRegisteredDynamicCategory
functions.signature: static inline struct PerfettoTeCategory PerfettoTeRegisteredDynamicCategory(void)
functions.description: Returns a synthetic category object representing any dynamic category, used when dynamic categories are passed as extra parameters. It references the global "any category" enable state and impl.
requirements: No input requirements. The returned category is intended for dynamic category checks, not for registration or mutation.

functions.name: PerfettoTeLlBeginSlowPath
functions.signature: static inline struct PerfettoTeLlIterator PerfettoTeLlBeginSlowPath(struct PerfettoTeCategory* cat, struct PerfettoTeTimestamp ts)
functions.description: Begins iterating over active instances of the low-level data source for the given category at the provided timestamp, returning an iterator object to use with subsequent calls.
requirements: cat must be a non-null pointer to a registered category (uses cat->impl).
ts must contain a valid timestamp and clock id as expected by the backend.

functions.name: PerfettoTeLlNext
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoTeLlNext(struct PerfettoTeCategory* cat, struct PerfettoTeTimestamp ts, struct PerfettoTeLlIterator* iterator)
functions.description: Advances the iterator over active low-level data source instances for the category at the provided timestamp.
requirements: cat must be a non-null pointer to a registered category (uses cat->impl).
iterator must be a non-null pointer previously obtained from PerfettoTeLlBeginSlowPath.
ts must contain a valid timestamp.

functions.name: PerfettoTeLlBreak
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoTeLlBreak(struct PerfettoTeCategory* cat, struct PerfettoTeLlIterator* iterator)
functions.description: Stops iteration early if there is an active tracer, informing the backend to end the iteration for this category/iterator.
requirements: cat must be a non-null pointer to a registered category (uses cat->impl).
iterator must be a non-null pointer previously obtained from PerfettoTeLlBeginSlowPath.

functions.name: PerfettoTeLlDynCatEnabled
functions.signature: static inline bool PerfettoTeLlDynCatEnabled(struct PerfettoTeLlIterator* iterator, const struct PerfettoTeCategoryDescriptor* dyn_cat)
functions.description: Checks whether the given dynamic category descriptor is enabled in the current active data source instance referenced by iterator.
requirements: iterator must be a non-null pointer obtained via PerfettoTeLlBeginSlowPath/PerfettoTeLlNext and still valid.
dyn_cat must be a non-null pointer to a category descriptor when checking a specific dynamic category.

functions.name: PerfettoTeLlPacketBegin
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoTeLlPacketBegin(struct PerfettoTeLlIterator* iterator, struct PerfettoDsRootTracePacket* root)
