functions.description: Initializes a new TracePacket for the current data source instance referenced by iterator and prepares the root protobuf message writer for serialization.
requirements: iterator must be a non-null pointer referencing a valid active data source instance.
root must be a non-null pointer to storage for the output packet/writer.
Must be paired with a corresponding PerfettoTeLlPacketEnd on the same iterator/root before reuse.

functions.name: PerfettoTeLlPacketEnd
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoTeLlPacketEnd(struct PerfettoTeLlIterator* iterator, struct PerfettoDsRootTracePacket* root)
functions.description: Finalizes the protobuf message for the packet initialized by PerfettoTeLlPacketBegin and ends the packet on the tracer.
requirements: Must be called after PerfettoTeLlPacketBegin with the same iterator/root.
iterator and root must be non-null and valid until the call completes.
Do not use root to write further fields after this call.

functions.name: PerfettoTeLlFlushPacket
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoTeLlFlushPacket(struct PerfettoTeLlIterator* iterator)
functions.description: Flushes the current tracer associated with the iterator, emitting any buffered packet data.
requirements: iterator must be a non-null pointer referencing a valid data source instance.

functions.name: PerfettoTeLlTrackSeen
functions.signature: static inline bool PerfettoTeLlTrackSeen(struct PerfettoTeLlImplIncr* incr, uint64_t uuid)
functions.description: Returns whether the incremental state has previously observed a track with the given UUID.
requirements: incr must be a non-null pointer to a valid incremental state object.

functions.name: PerfettoTeLlIntern
functions.signature: static inline uint64_t PerfettoTeLlIntern(struct PerfettoTeLlImplIncr* incr, int32_t type, const void* data, size_t data_size, bool* seen)
functions.description: Interns arbitrary data under a specific InternedData type, returning a stable interned id (iid). Sets *seen to false if the data was not previously interned for that type.
requirements: incr must be a non-null pointer to a valid incremental state object.
type must correspond to a field id in perfetto.protos.InternedData (explicit).
data must point to a buffer of at least data_size bytes; data may be reused by caller after the call.
seen must be a non-null pointer to a bool for result output.

functions.name: PerfettoTeLlInternContextInit
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoTeLlInternContextInit(struct PerfettoTeLlInternContext* ctx, struct PerfettoTeLlImplIncr* incr, struct perfetto_protos_TracePacket* tp)
functions.description: Initializes an interning context to lazily create and populate the InternedData submessage within a TracePacket using the provided incremental state pointer.
requirements: ctx must be a non-null pointer.
incr must be a non-null pointer to a valid incremental state object.
tp must be a non-null pointer to an initialized TracePacket message ready for submessages.

functions.name: PerfettoTeLlInternContextStartIfNeeded
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoTeLlInternContextStartIfNeeded(struct PerfettoTeLlInternContext* ctx)
functions.description: Starts the InternedData submessage within the TracePacket if it hasn't been started yet. Safe to call multiple times; it only starts once.
requirements: ctx must be a non-null pointer previously initialized with PerfettoTeLlInternContextInit.
ctx->tp must be valid; ctx->incr should remain valid for subsequent interning calls.

functions.name: PerfettoTeLlInternContextDestroy
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoTeLlInternContextDestroy(struct PerfettoTeLlInternContext* ctx)
functions.description: Finalizes the InternedData submessage if it was started, closing the nested message within the TracePacket.
requirements: ctx must be a non-null pointer previously initialized with PerfettoTeLlInternContextInit.
Must be called after all interning using this context is complete and before finalizing the TracePacket.

functions.name: PerfettoTeLlInternRegisteredCat
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoTeLlInternRegisteredCat(struct PerfettoTeLlInternContext* ctx, struct PerfettoTeCategory* reg_cat)
functions.description: Ensures the registered category is interned: interns its category iid into the incremental state and, if newly seen, writes the EventCategory message (name and iid) into the InternedData submessage.
requirements: ctx must be a non-null pointer initialized via PerfettoTeLlInternContextInit (ctx->incr and ctx->tp valid for the packet's lifetime).
reg_cat must be a non-null pointer to a registered category; if reg_cat->cat_iid is 0, the function returns without writing.
Caller must ensure PerfettoTeLlInternContextDestroy is called later if this function started the InternedData submessage.

functions.name: PerfettoTeLlWriteRegisteredCat
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoTeLlWriteRegisteredCat(struct perfetto_protos_TrackEvent* te, struct PerfettoTeCategory* reg_cat)
functions.description: Writes the category onto a TrackEvent either by setting the interned category iid (preferred) or, if not available, by setting the category name directly.
requirements: te must be a non-null pointer to an initialized TrackEvent message.
reg_cat must be a non-null pointer; it should have either cat_iid set or desc.name set for output.

functions.name: PerfettoTeLlWriteDynamicCat
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoTeLlWriteDynamicCat(struct perfetto_protos_TrackEvent* te, struct PerfettoTeCategoryDescriptor* dyn_cat, int32_t type)
functions.description: Writes a dynamic category name into the TrackEvent if provided and if the event type is not SLICE_END or COUNTER; otherwise does nothing.
requirements: te must be a non-null pointer to an initialized TrackEvent message.
dyn_cat may be NULL; when non-null, dyn_cat->name should be a valid NUL-terminated string.
type must be a valid Perfetto track event type; for PERFETTO_TE_TYPE_SLICE_END and PERFETTO_TE_TYPE_COUNTER the function intentionally does not write the category.

functions.name: PerfettoTeLlInternEventName
functions.signature: static inline uint64_t PerfettoTeLlInternEventName(struct PerfettoTeLlInternContext* ctx, const char* name)
functions.description: Interns an event name string and returns its iid. If the name was newly interned, emits the corresponding EventName message into the InternedData submessage. Returns 0 if name is NULL.
requirements: ctx must be a non-null pointer initialized via PerfettoTeLlInternContextInit.
If name is non-null, it must be a NUL-terminated C string.

functions.name: PerfettoTeLlWriteEventName
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoTeLlWriteEventName(struct perfetto_protos_TrackEvent* te, const char* name)
functions.description: Writes an event name directly into a TrackEvent if name is non-null.
requirements: te must be a non-null pointer to an initialized TrackEvent message.
If name is non-null, it must be a NUL-terminated C string.

functions.name: PerfettoTeLlWriteInternedEventName
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoTeLlWriteInternedEventName(struct perfetto_protos_TrackEvent* te, uint64_t iid)
functions.description: Writes an interned event name iid into a TrackEvent if iid is non-zero.
requirements: te must be a non-null pointer to an initialized TrackEvent message.
iid should be a valid non-zero intern id previously returned by interning APIs.

functions.name: PerfettoTeLlWriteTimestamp
functions.signature: static inline void PerfettoTeLlWriteTimestamp(struct perfetto_protos_TracePacket* tp, const struct PerfettoTeTimestamp* ts)
functions.description: Writes a timestamp and its clock id into a TracePacket.
requirements: tp must be a non-null pointer to an initialized TracePacket message.
ts must be a non-null pointer; ts->value and ts->clock_id must be set appropriately for the trace.

functions.name: PerfettoTeLlInternDbgArgName
functions.signature: static inline uint64_t PerfettoTeLlInternDbgArgName(struct PerfettoTeLlInternContext* ctx, const char* name)
functions.description: Interns a debug annotation name string and returns its iid. If newly interned, emits the corresponding EventName message into the InternedData submessage. Returns 0 if name is NULL.
requirements: ctx must be a non-null pointer initialized via PerfettoTeLlInternContextInit.
If name is non-null, it must be a NUL-terminated C string.

functions.name: PerfettoGetThreadId
functions.signature: static inline PerfettoThreadId PerfettoGetThreadId(void)
functions.description: Returns the OS/kernel thread identifier of the calling thread. On Bionic-based Android it calls gettid(), on Linux/glibc it uses syscall(__NR_gettid) with a cast to PerfettoThreadId, and on other platforms it delegates to PerfettoGetThreadIdImpl() provided by the Perfetto ABI. Use this to obtain a stable per-thread ID for logging, tracing, or correlation within the process. No arguments; executes in the caller’s thread and returns its ID.
requirements: Include perfetto/public/thread_utils.h (and transitively perfetto/public/abi/thread_utils_abi.h) before use.
On non-Linux platforms, ensure the build links/includes the implementation of PerfettoGetThreadIdImpl() supplied by the Perfetto ABI; otherwise this symbol must be available.
Callable from any thread; it returns the ID of the calling thread.
No parameters are required; the return value is the thread identifier of type PerfettoThreadId. No error reporting is defined.

functions.name: PerfettoHeapBufferCreate
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT struct PerfettoHeapBuffer* PerfettoHeapBufferCreate(struct PerfettoStreamWriter*);
functions.description: Creates a new heap-backed buffer that can be used with PerfettoStreamWriter to serialize protobuf data. The caller supplies a pointer to an uninitialized PerfettoStreamWriter that the heap buffer setup will use; the writer can then be used to write into the heap buffer. Returns a handle to the created PerfettoHeapBuffer, which must later be destroyed with PerfettoHeapBufferDestroy. Notes: documentation implies the provided writer is owned by the caller and is expected to be tied to the created buffer thereafter.
requirements: The PerfettoStreamWriter* argument must be a valid pointer to an uninitialized PerfettoStreamWriter (explicitly stated).
The PerfettoStreamWriter passed remains owned by the caller (explicitly stated).
The returned PerfettoHeapBuffer* must be destroyed via PerfettoHeapBufferDestroy when no longer needed (inferred from API pairing).
Do not pass a null PerfettoStreamWriter pointer (inferred from requirement that it must be uninitialized, not absent).
The function should be called before attempting to serialize data into the buffer via the associated PerfettoStreamWriter (inferred from usage).

functions.name: PerfettoHeapBufferCopyInto
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT void PerfettoHeapBufferCopyInto(struct PerfettoHeapBuffer*, struct PerfettoStreamWriter*, void* dst, size_t size);
functions.description: Copies serialized data from the heap buffer into the caller-provided destination buffer, up to size bytes. Intended to retrieve data previously written via the associated PerfettoStreamWriter. Behavior when size exceeds the available data is not documented; callers typically choose size to match the amount of buffered data they intend to copy.
requirements: The PerfettoHeapBuffer* must be a valid buffer previously created by PerfettoHeapBufferCreate (inferred from API).
The PerfettoStreamWriter* should be the same writer associated with the PerfettoHeapBuffer (inferred from matching parameter across API).
dst must point to a writable memory region of at least size bytes (inferred from typical copy semantics).
If size is greater than 0, dst must not be NULL (inferred).
The function should be called only after data has been written into the buffer if the caller expects meaningful output (inferred).

functions.name: PerfettoHeapBufferDestroy
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT void PerfettoHeapBufferDestroy(struct PerfettoHeapBuffer*, struct PerfettoStreamWriter*);
functions.description: Destroys and frees resources associated with a PerfettoHeapBuffer created by PerfettoHeapBufferCreate. Takes the associated PerfettoStreamWriter as an argument, which remains owned by the caller. After this call, the buffer handle must not be used.
requirements: The PerfettoHeapBuffer* must have been created by PerfettoHeapBufferCreate and not previously destroyed (inferred).
The PerfettoStreamWriter* should be the same writer originally provided at creation (inferred from API symmetry).
After destruction, the PerfettoHeapBuffer* must not be used again (inferred).
Do not pass NULL pointers (inferred: API does not document acceptance of NULL).

functions.name: PerfettoPbDecoderParseField
functions.signature: struct PerfettoPbDecoderField PerfettoPbDecoderParseField(struct PerfettoPbDecoder* decoder);
functions.description: Parses the next protobuf field from the decoder’s buffer and returns a PerfettoPbDecoderField describing it (including status, wire type, id, and value). On success, advances decoder->read_ptr to the byte immediately after the parsed field. Use this in a loop to iterate fields of a length-delimited protobuf message held in a contiguous memory buffer. Inspect the returned field.status for PERFETTO_PB_DECODER_OK, PERFETTO_PB_DECODER_DONE (no more data), or PERFETTO_PB_DECODER_ERROR (decoding failed; read_ptr not advanced).
requirements: decoder must be a valid, non-null pointer.
decoder->read_ptr and decoder->end_ptr must delimit a valid, contiguous memory buffer containing a protobuf-encoded message segment (read_ptr <= end_ptr).
Before the first call, initialize decoder->read_ptr to the start of the buffer and decoder->end_ptr to one past the end.
Caller must check the returned field.status and handle PERFETTO_PB_DECODER_OK, PERFETTO_PB_DECODER_DONE, and PERFETTO_PB_DECODER_ERROR appropriately.
On PERFETTO_PB_DECODER_ERROR, do not assume decoder->read_ptr advanced (it is not updated).
The returned field’s value union member is only valid according to the reported wire_type (e.g., use .delimited for wire type 2, integer64 for 0/1, integer32 or float_val for 5, double_val for 1).

functions.name: PerfettoPbDecoderSkipField
functions.signature: uint32_t PerfettoPbDecoderSkipField(struct PerfettoPbDecoder* decoder);
functions.description: Skips over the next protobuf field without decoding its contents, advancing decoder->read_ptr to the byte after that field. Returns a PerfettoPbDecoderStatus indicating whether a field was skipped (OK), no more data was present (DONE), or an error occurred (ERROR). Use when you want to ignore unknown or unwanted fields while scanning a message.
requirements: decoder must be a valid, non-null pointer.
decoder->read_ptr and decoder->end_ptr must delimit a valid, contiguous memory buffer (read_ptr <= end_ptr).
Before the first call, initialize decoder->read_ptr to the start of the buffer and decoder->end_ptr to one past the end.
Caller must check the return status (PERFETTO_PB_DECODER_OK, PERFETTO_PB_DECODER_DONE, or PERFETTO_PB_DECODER_ERROR) and branch accordingly.
On PERFETTO_PB_DECODER_ERROR, do not assume decoder->read_ptr advanced (it is not updated).

functions.name: PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgsCreate
functions.signature: struct PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgs* PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgsCreate(void);
functions.description: Creates a new opaque PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgs object used to hold configuration parameters for initializing a producer backend. Typical usage: call this to obtain a config object, set options on it (e.g., shared memory size hint), pass it to one of the init functions, then destroy it.
requirements: Must be called before using the returned PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgs with other API functions.
The returned pointer represents an allocated, opaque configuration object and must later be released with PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgsDestroy.

functions.name: PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgsSetShmemSizeHintKb
functions.signature: void PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgsSetShmemSizeHintKb(struct PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgs* args, uint32_t size);
functions.description: Sets a hint for the shared memory buffer size (between the current process and the tracing service backend(s)) on the provided init-args object. This tunes the trade-off between memory footprint and ability to sustain bursts of trace writes. The function name indicates the unit is kilobytes; the comment specifies the value must be a multiple of 4 KB and may be ignored if too large or misaligned.
requirements: args must be a valid pointer to a PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgs previously created by PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgsCreate and not yet destroyed.
size is a size hint in kilobytes (inferred from the function name).
size must be a multiple of 4 KB (i.e., the overall size must be 4 KB-aligned).
If size is larger than kMaxShmSize (32 MB) or not a multiple of 4 KB, the hint can be ignored by the implementation.

functions.name: PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgsDestroy
functions.signature: void PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgsDestroy(struct PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgs* args);
functions.description: Destroys (frees) a PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgs object previously created with PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgsCreate. Use after initialization is complete or when the args object is no longer needed.
requirements: args must be a valid pointer returned by PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgsCreate.
Do not use the args object after it has been destroyed.
Only destroy each PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgs object once (inferred standard lifecycle requirement).

functions.name: PerfettoProducerSystemInit
functions.signature: void PerfettoProducerSystemInit(const struct PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgs* args);
functions.description: Initializes the global system Perfetto producer using the provided init arguments. Safe to call multiple times; if the producer is already initialized, most of the arguments are ignored. The function does not take ownership of args; the args object can be destroyed immediately after this call returns.
requirements: args must point to a valid PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgs configured as desired.
It is acceptable to call this function multiple times; repeated calls will ignore most args if already initialized (as documented).
The args object is not owned by the callee and may be destroyed immediately after the call returns.

functions.name: PerfettoProducerInProcessInit
functions.signature: void PerfettoProducerInProcessInit(const struct PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgs* args);
functions.description: Initializes the global in-process Perfetto producer using the provided init arguments. Safe to call multiple times; if already initialized, most arguments are ignored. The function does not take ownership of args; the args object can be destroyed immediately after this call returns.
requirements: args must point to a valid PerfettoProducerBackendInitArgs configured as desired.
It is acceptable to call this function multiple times; repeated calls will ignore most args if already initialized (as documented).
The args object is not owned by the callee and may be destroyed immediately after the call returns.

functions.name: PerfettoProducerActivateTriggers
functions.signature: void PerfettoProducerActivateTriggers(const char* trigger_names[], uint32_t ttl_ms);
functions.description: Informs the tracing services to activate any of the given triggers for sessions waiting on them. trigger_names must be an array of C strings (each zero-terminated), with the last pointer in the array set to NULL to mark the end. The trigger signal is sent to all initialized backends that are currently connected and those that connect within the next ttl_ms milliseconds; the function returns immediately.
requirements: trigger_names must be a valid array of pointers to zero-terminated C strings, terminated by a NULL pointer as the last element.
Each non-NULL trigger_names[i] must point to a valid, readable, zero-terminated string for the duration of the call.
ttl_ms specifies a time window in milliseconds during which newly connecting backends also receive the trigger.

functions.name: PerfettoStreamWriterUpdateWritePtr
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT void PerfettoStreamWriterUpdateWritePtr(struct PerfettoStreamWriter*);
functions.description: Advances/commits the write position for the current chunk. The function tells the writer that all bytes up to writer->write_ptr (non-inclusive) are now valid data, updating the internal state accordingly. Typical usage: after writing data directly into the chunk’s buffer, set writer->write_ptr to the first unwritten byte and call this function to commit that progress.
requirements: writer must be a non-null, initialized PerfettoStreamWriter.
writer->begin, writer->write_ptr, and writer->end must describe a valid current chunk with begin <= write_ptr <= end (per struct contract).
The caller should set writer->write_ptr to the intended commit position within the current chunk before calling.
No return value; callers must not expect error reporting from this API.

functions.name: PerfettoStreamWriterNewChunk
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT void PerfettoStreamWriterNewChunk(struct PerfettoStreamWriter*);
functions.description: Commits the current chunk and acquires a new chunk for subsequent writes. Intended to be called when the current chunk is complete or lacks sufficient space for further data.
requirements: writer must be a non-null, initialized PerfettoStreamWriter.

If any bytes were written into the current chunk, the caller should have updated writer->write_ptr to the correct position and called PerfettoStreamWriterUpdateWritePtr beforehand (to ensure all written data is committed).
After this call returns, writer->begin, writer->end, and writer->write_ptr will refer to the new chunk; any direct pointers into the old chunk become invalid unless redirected via AnnotatePatch.
No return value; callers must not expect error reporting from this API.

functions.name: PerfettoStreamWriterAppendBytesSlowpath
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT void PerfettoStreamWriterAppendBytesSlowpath(struct PerfettoStreamWriter*, const uint8_t* src, size_t size);
functions.description: Appends size bytes from src to the stream writer, handling slow-path conditions (e.g., insufficient remaining space) by committing the current chunk and/or acquiring new chunks as needed.
requirements: writer must be a non-null, initialized PerfettoStreamWriter.
If size > 0, src must be non-null and point to at least size bytes readable by the caller.
It is safe to pass size == 0; in that case src is ignored.
The function may span multiple chunks; callers must not assume contiguity of appended data across chunk boundaries.
The caller must not rely on any direct pointer into the current chunk remaining valid across this call, as it may commit and replace the chunk.
No return value; callers must not expect error reporting from this API.

functions.name: PerfettoStreamWriterAnnotatePatch
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT uint8_t* PerfettoStreamWriterAnnotatePatch(struct PerfettoStreamWriter*, uint8_t* patch_addr);
functions.description: Marks a 4-byte patch region within the current chunk for later backfilling after the chunk is finalized. If necessary, the stream writer redirects the patch to a safe location and returns the address where the caller should eventually write the patch. The first byte written to the returned location must be non-zero. This is commonly used to backfill sizes of protozero messages.
requirements: writer must be a non-null, initialized PerfettoStreamWriter.
patch_addr must point to a region within the current chunk and cover PERFETTO_STREAM_WRITER_PATCH_SIZE (4) contiguous bytes starting at patch_addr.
The caller must only write to the returned location after the current chunk has been committed/replaced ("after the current chunk has gone away").
If the function returns NULL, the caller must not write anything for this patch.
When writing the patch, the first byte written must be non-zero.
The caller should not write more than PERFETTO_STREAM_WRITER_PATCH_SIZE (4) bytes to the returned location.

functions.name: PerfettoStreamWriterReserveBytesSlowpath
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT void PerfettoStreamWriterReserveBytesSlowpath(struct PerfettoStreamWriter*, size_t size);
functions.description: Ensures that an area of length size is reserved in the current chunk for writing and considered committed by the writer (i.e., the reserved region will not be reused). This is the slow-path helper used when a simple inline reservation cannot be satisfied (e.g., due to insufficient remaining space).
requirements: writer must be a non-null, initialized PerfettoStreamWriter.
size must be smaller than the chunk size provided by the writer’s delegate (per header warning); otherwise behavior is unsupported.
The function may commit the current chunk and acquire a new chunk to satisfy the reservation; any prior direct pointers into the chunk may become invalid.
No return value; the actual pointer to the reserved area is managed by the writer implementation/fast path; callers should not expect this function to return a pointer directly.

functions.name: PerfettoGetThreadIdImpl
functions.signature: PerfettoThreadId PerfettoGetThreadIdImpl(void);
functions.description: Returns the operating-system specific identifier for the calling thread. The return type PerfettoThreadId is platform-dependent: on Linux it is pid_t (thread ID as returned by gettid semantics), on Fuchsia zx_koid_t, on Apple/Windows uint64_t, and otherwise pthread_t. Typical usage is to call this from any code that needs a stable, comparable identifier for the current thread for logging, tracing, or correlation. Exact semantics (e.g., size and comparability across processes) depend on the platform; treat the value as an opaque thread identifier.

functions.name: PerfettoTracingSessionSystemCreate
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT struct PerfettoTracingSessionImpl* PerfettoTracingSessionSystemCreate(void);
functions.description: Creates a new tracing session connected to the system Perfetto service. Returns an opaque session handle used by subsequent setup/start/stop/read/destroy APIs. Typical usage: create, setup with a serialized TraceConfig, start, stop, optionally flush, read the trace, then destroy.
requirements: Return value: a non-null pointer indicates session creation succeeded; null indicates failure (behavior not documented in header).
The returned session handle is opaque and must be passed unchanged to other session APIs from this header.
Exactly one matching PerfettoTracingSessionDestroy() must be called to release the session when finished.
Thread-safety and ownership semantics are not documented; assume the handle must not be used after destroy.
No configuration is provided at creation; caller must call PerfettoTracingSessionSetup() before starting the session (inferred from API shape).

functions.name: PerfettoTracingSessionInProcessCreate
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT struct PerfettoTracingSessionImpl* PerfettoTracingSessionInProcessCreate(void);
functions.description: Creates a new tracing session for in-process tracing (not using the system service). Returns an opaque session handle for subsequent operations. Typical usage mirrors the system create path: create, setup, start, stop/flush, read, destroy.
requirements: Return value: non-null indicates success; null indicates failure (behavior not documented in header).
The returned handle is opaque and must be passed unchanged to other APIs from this header.
Exactly one matching PerfettoTracingSessionDestroy() must be called to release the session.
Must call PerfettoTracingSessionSetup() before starting (inferred from API shape).
Choice between SystemCreate and InProcessCreate determines where the session runs; they are not interchangeable for a single session.

functions.name: PerfettoTracingSessionSetup
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT void PerfettoTracingSessionSetup(struct PerfettoTracingSessionImpl* , void* cfg_begin, size_t cfg_len);
functions.description: Configures a tracing session with a serialized trace configuration buffer supplied by the caller. The buffer at cfg_begin of length cfg_len is interpreted by Perfetto as the TraceConfig for the session. Expected to be called before starting the session.
requirements: The first parameter must be a valid session handle obtained from one of the create functions and not yet destroyed.
cfg_begin must point to a readable memory buffer at least cfg_len bytes long for the duration of the call.
cfg_len must correctly describe the size of the configuration buffer; zero-length configuration semantics are unspecified.
Must be called before starting the session with StartAsync/StartBlocking (inferred from name and API flow).
The format/layout of the configuration buffer must match the Perfetto TraceConfig serialization expected by this ABI (exact format not documented here).

functions.name: PerfettoTracingSessionSetStopCb
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT void PerfettoTracingSessionSetStopCb(struct PerfettoTracingSessionImpl* , PerfettoTracingSessionStopCb cb, void* user_arg);
functions.description: Registers a callback to be invoked when the tracing session is stopped. The callback receives the session handle and the user_arg provided here. Useful to be notified asynchronously after a stop request completes.
requirements: The session handle must be valid and not destroyed.
cb should be a valid function pointer; behavior if cb is NULL is unspecified by this header.
The callback may be invoked asynchronously; it must be reentrant-safe and avoid calling APIs that are not safe from that context (exact threading model not fully specified).
user_arg is passed verbatim to the callback and is not inspected by the API; the caller must ensure its lifetime outlives potential callback invocations.

functions.name: PerfettoTracingSessionStartAsync
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT void PerfettoTracingSessionStartAsync(struct PerfettoTracingSessionImpl* );
functions.description: Starts the configured tracing session asynchronously and returns immediately. Use when you do not need to block for the start to complete.
requirements: The session handle must be valid and configured via PerfettoTracingSessionSetup() (inferred).
Should not be called after the session has been destroyed.
Do not assume tracing has begun synchronously upon return; if start completion matters, prefer StartBlocking or use appropriate synchronization (inferred).

functions.name: PerfettoTracingSessionStartBlocking
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT void PerfettoTracingSessionStartBlocking(struct PerfettoTracingSessionImpl* );
functions.description: Starts the configured tracing session and blocks until the start operation completes.
requirements: The session handle must be valid and configured via PerfettoTracingSessionSetup() (inferred).
Should not be called after the session has been destroyed.

functions.name: PerfettoTracingSessionStopAsync
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT void PerfettoTracingSessionStopAsync(struct PerfettoTracingSessionImpl* );
functions.description: Requests the tracing session to stop asynchronously and returns immediately. Pair with PerfettoTracingSessionSetStopCb() to be notified when the session has fully stopped.
requirements: The session handle must be valid.
If a stop callback was set with PerfettoTracingSessionSetStopCb(), it may be invoked asynchronously when the stop completes; ensure the callback and user data remain valid until then.
Should not be called after destruction; behavior when called on an already-stopped session is unspecified.

functions.name: PerfettoTracingSessionStopBlocking
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT void PerfettoTracingSessionStopBlocking(struct PerfettoTracingSessionImpl* );
functions.description: Stops the tracing session and blocks until the stop completes.
requirements: The session handle must be valid.
Should not be called after destruction; behavior when called on an already-stopped session is unspecified.

functions.name: PerfettoTracingSessionFlushAsync
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT void PerfettoTracingSessionFlushAsync(struct PerfettoTracingSessionImpl* , uint32_t timeout_ms, PerfettoTracingSessionFlushCb cb, void* user_arg);
functions.description: Issues an asynchronous flush request to data sources, acting as a fence so data written before the call becomes visible in the trace buffer and to PerfettoTracingSessionReadTraceBlocking(). Returns immediately and invokes cb when all data sources ack the flush or the timeout elapses.
requirements: The session handle must be valid.
timeout_ms is in milliseconds; if 0, the service uses the TraceConfig flush_timeout_ms, or a 5s default if unspecified (per documentation).
cb must be a valid function pointer. It will be invoked on an internal Perfetto thread when the flush completes or times out.
The callback receives a boolean success indicating whether all data sources acknowledged before timeout; caller must handle both outcomes.
user_arg is passed verbatim to the callback; it must remain valid until the callback runs.
Because the callback runs on an internal thread, it must be thread-safe and should return promptly to avoid delaying internal operations.

functions.name: PerfettoTracingSessionFlushBlocking
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT bool PerfettoTracingSessionFlushBlocking(struct PerfettoTracingSessionImpl* , uint32_t timeout_ms);
functions.description: Synchronously issues a flush request and blocks until all data sources acknowledge or the timeout elapses. Returns true on success (all acks), false on timeout or error.
requirements: The session handle must be valid.
timeout_ms is in milliseconds; if 0, the service uses the TraceConfig flush_timeout_ms, or a 5s default if unspecified (per documentation).
Caller must check the boolean return to detect timeout or error and handle it appropriately.

functions.name: PerfettoTracingSessionReadTraceBlocking
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT void PerfettoTracingSessionReadTraceBlocking(struct PerfettoTracingSessionImpl* , PerfettoTracingSessionReadCb cb, void* user_arg);
functions.description: Reads trace data from the session and repeatedly invokes cb with contiguous chunks of data. Blocks until all currently available trace data is delivered. Each callback invocation receives a pointer to data, its size, and a has_more flag indicating whether more chunks will follow.
requirements: The session handle must be valid.
cb must be a valid function pointer. It will be called multiple times with data pointers valid only for the duration of the call (lifetime not explicitly stated; treat as transient).
user_arg is passed verbatim to cb and must remain valid for the duration of the read.
The callback must be prepared to handle has_more being true for intermediate chunks and false for the final chunk.
For deterministic visibility of data written before a point, issue a flush (FlushAsync/FlushBlocking) prior to reading as needed (per documentation note about flush as a fence).
The function blocks the calling thread until reading completes; avoid calling from a thread that must remain responsive.

functions.name: PerfettoTracingSessionDestroy
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT void PerfettoTracingSessionDestroy(struct PerfettoTracingSessionImpl* );
functions.description: Destroys and releases a tracing session created by one of the create functions. After this call the session handle must not be used.
requirements: The session handle must be either null or a valid handle created by this API; using the handle after destroy is invalid. Behavior on double-destroy is unspecified.
Should be called exactly once for each successfully created session to avoid leaks.
Ensure no callbacks (stop or flush) will access the session after destruction; if callbacks may still fire, coordinate shutdown to avoid use-after-free (threading model not specified).

functions.name: PerfettoTeInit
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT void PerfettoTeInit(void);
functions.description: Initializes the Perfetto Track Event (TE) subsystem. Intended to set up any necessary global state before using other track event APIs. Details of idempotency and side effects are not documented.
requirements: May need to be called before using other Perfetto TE category and event APIs (inferred from Init naming).
Thread-safety, idempotency, and error reporting are unknown (not documented).

functions.name: PerfettoTeCategoryImplCreate
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT struct PerfettoTeCategoryImpl* PerfettoTeCategoryImplCreate(struct PerfettoTeCategoryDescriptor* desc);
functions.description: Registers a track event category with the tracing service using the provided descriptor and returns an opaque handle to the registered category.
requirements: desc must remain alive, along with all objects it points to (name, desc, tags contents), until PerfettoTeCategoryImplDestroy() is called (explicit).

desc should describe a category: name is a null-terminated string; desc (description) is a null-terminated string; tags is an array of pointers to null-terminated strings or NULL if num_tags == 0; num_tags is the number of elements in tags (explicit from struct comments).
desc should be a valid, initialized descriptor (inferred from function purpose).
Return value must be checked for NULL if the caller needs to detect registration failure (not documented whether NULL can be returned).

functions.name: PerfettoTePublishCategories
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT void PerfettoTePublishCategories(void);
functions.description: Notifies the tracing service about category registration changes after categories have been created or destroyed.
requirements: Must be called after one or more calls to PerfettoTeCategoryImplCreate() or PerfettoTeCategoryImplDestroy() to publish changes (explicit).
May be called multiple times as needed after batches of changes (inferred from wording).

functions.name: PerfettoTeCategoryImplGetEnabled
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT PERFETTO_ATOMIC(bool)* PerfettoTeCategoryImplGetEnabled(struct PerfettoTeCategoryImpl* cat);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to an atomic boolean indicating whether the given category is currently enabled. The returned pointer remains valid until the category is destroyed.
requirements: cat must reference a valid, registered category that has not been destroyed (explicit).
The returned pointer must not be dereferenced after the category is destroyed (explicit).
Atomic access semantics should be respected when reading/writing via PERFETTO_ATOMIC(bool) (inferred from type).

functions.name: PerfettoTeCategoryImplSetCallback
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT void PerfettoTeCategoryImplSetCallback(struct PerfettoTeCategoryImpl* cat, PerfettoTeCategoryImplCallback cb, void* user_arg);
functions.description: Registers or clears a callback to be invoked whenever a data source instance with the specified category is created or destroyed. The provided user_arg is passed through to the callback. Passing NULL for cb disables the callback.
requirements: cat must reference a valid, registered category (inferred).
cb may be NULL to disable the callback (explicit).
The callback signature must match: void (*)(struct PerfettoTeCategoryImpl*, PerfettoDsInstanceIndex inst_id, bool created, bool global_state_changed, void* user_arg) (explicit typedef).
The callback must tolerate being called on both creation (created=true) and destruction (created=false) events; global_state_changed indicates first enablement or last disablement (explicit).
Threading and reentrancy guarantees for the callback are not documented; the callback should be thread-safe (inferred as a safe practice).

functions.name: PerfettoTeCategoryImplGetIid
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT uint64_t PerfettoTeCategoryImplGetIid(struct PerfettoTeCategoryImpl* cat);
functions.description: Retrieves the interning ID (iid) associated with the registered category. Useful for low-level integrations that need a stable identifier for the category.
requirements: cat must reference a valid, registered category (inferred).
Behavior if cat is NULL or invalid is not documented; caller should avoid passing invalid pointers (inferred).

functions.name: PerfettoTeCategoryImplDestroy
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT void PerfettoTeCategoryImplDestroy(struct PerfettoTeCategoryImpl* cat);
functions.description: Destroys a previously registered category. After destruction, the category must not be used for tracing or in any API that requires a live category.
requirements: cat must be a category previously returned by PerfettoTeCategoryImplCreate (inferred).
Do not use the category or any pointers derived from it (e.g., from PerfettoTeCategoryImplGetEnabled) after destruction (explicit).
Do not destroy the same category more than once (inferred).
After destroying at least one category, call PerfettoTePublishCategories() to notify the service of changes (explicit from the publish function’s contract).

functions.name: PerfettoTeGetTimestamp
functions.signature: PERFETTO_SDK_EXPORT struct PerfettoTeTimestamp PerfettoTeGetTimestamp(void);
functions.description: Obtains the current timestamp as a PerfettoTeTimestamp containing a clock_id (PerfettoTeTimestampType) and its value.
requirements: No input arguments or preconditions are documented.
The meaning of clock_id values is defined by PerfettoTeTimestampType; consumers should handle the returned clock domain appropriately (explicit via enum).

functions.name: PerfettoTeHlEmitImpl
functions.signature: void PerfettoTeHlEmitImpl(struct PerfettoTeCategoryImpl* cat, int32_t type, const char* name, struct PerfettoTeHlExtra* const* extra_data);
functions.description: Emits a track event to all active instances of the Perfetto track event data source. Call exactly once per tracepoint, providing all data needed for that event; the function iterates enabled data source instances and serializes the event as protobuf messages. Use with a registered category (or the special dynamic-category handle) and optionally supply a name and additional parameters via an array of extra-data descriptors. This high-level API covers common track-event cases; custom protobuf payloads can be provided via the proto-fields extra types.
requirements: cat must point to a valid PerfettoTeCategoryImpl corresponding to a registered category; for dynamic categories, use the special perfetto_te_all_categories handle (as documented).
type must be a valid value of enum PerfettoTeType (e.g., slice begin/end, etc.).
If type is PERFETTO_TE_TYPE_SLICE_END, name must be NULL (slice end events cannot have a name). For other event types, name may be NULL or a valid C string.
extra_data must be an array of pointers to PerfettoTeHlExtra-derived structs and must be terminated by a NULL pointer.
Each element in extra_data must begin with PerfettoTeHlExtra header and have header.type set to the matching enum PerfettoTeHlExtraType for the concrete struct provided.

functions.name: PerfettoTeLlImplBegin
functions.signature: struct PerfettoTeLlImplIterator PerfettoTeLlImplBegin(struct PerfettoTeCategoryImpl* cat, struct PerfettoTeTimestamp ts);
functions.description: Begins iteration over all active track event data source instances for the given category on the current thread. Returns an iterator; if iterator.ds.tracer is NULL, there are no active instances. Use with PerfettoTeLlImplNext to advance or PerfettoTeLlImplBreak to terminate early. Intended for low-level emission of track event protobufs per active instance.
requirements: cat must point to a valid PerfettoTeCategoryImpl for the category being queried.
ts must be a valid PerfettoTeTimestamp representing the current (or desired) timestamp for the iteration context.
Callers must check the returned iterator.ds.tracer; if NULL, iteration has no elements.
The iteration applies to active instances on the calling thread only.
The returned iterator is intended to be advanced with PerfettoTeLlImplNext and may be terminated with PerfettoTeLlImplBreak.

functions.name: PerfettoTeLlImplNext
functions.signature: void PerfettoTeLlImplNext(struct PerfettoTeCategoryImpl* cat, struct PerfettoTeTimestamp ts, struct PerfettoTeLlImplIterator* iterator);
functions.description: Advances the iterator to the next active track event data source instance for the given category. After the call, if iterator->ds.tracer is NULL, there are no more active instances. Used in a loop following PerfettoTeLlImplBegin to visit each active instance.
requirements: iterator must be a non-NULL pointer to an iterator previously returned by PerfettoTeLlImplBegin (and not yet terminated by PerfettoTeLlImplBreak).
cat must be the same category context used for iteration (a valid PerfettoTeCategoryImpl pointer).
ts must be a valid PerfettoTeTimestamp appropriate for the current step in iteration.
Callers must stop iterating when iterator->ds.tracer becomes NULL.

functions.name: PerfettoTeLlImplBreak
functions.signature: void PerfettoTeLlImplBreak(struct PerfettoTeCategoryImpl*, struct PerfettoTeLlImplIterator*);
functions.description: Prematurely terminates an iteration started by PerfettoTeLlImplBegin. Use to stop iterating before reaching the end.
requirements: Second parameter must be a non-NULL pointer to an iterator that was initialized by PerfettoTeLlImplBegin/PerfettoTeLlImplNext.
Must only be called to terminate an active iteration; the iterator should not be used after calling this function.
The category pointer must match the iteration’s category (opaque in the declaration; pass the same pointer used to begin iteration).

functions.name: PerfettoTeLlImplDynCatEnabled
functions.signature: bool PerfettoTeLlImplDynCatEnabled(struct PerfettoDsTracerImpl* tracer, PerfettoDsInstanceIndex inst_id, const struct PerfettoTeCategoryDescriptor* dyn_cat);
functions.description: Checks whether a dynamic category descriptor is enabled for the specified track event instance (identified by tracer and inst_id from the iterator). The descriptor does not need to be pre-registered.
requirements: tracer must be a valid pointer obtained from the iterator (iterator.ds.tracer).
inst_id must be the instance index associated with the iterator’s current element.
dyn_cat must point to a valid PerfettoTeCategoryDescriptor describing the dynamic category; it need not be registered in advance.

functions.name: PerfettoTeLlImplTrackSeen
functions.signature: bool PerfettoTeLlImplTrackSeen(struct PerfettoTeLlImplIncr*, uint64_t uuid);
functions.description: Returns true if the incremental state for the current track event instance has previously encountered the given track UUID. Useful to avoid re-emitting track metadata.
requirements: First parameter must be a valid pointer to the instance’s incremental state (e.g., iterator.incr).
uuid is a 64-bit track identifier; any uint64_t value is accepted.

functions.name: PerfettoTeLlImplIntern
functions.signature: uint64_t PerfettoTeLlImplIntern(struct PerfettoTeLlImplIncr* incr, int32_t type, const void* data, size_t data_size, bool* seen);
functions.description: Interns arbitrary data for a given interning type (a field id in perfetto.protos.InternedData), returning an interned id (iid). If this is the first time the data has been observed for that type, *seen is set to false; otherwise true. The returned iid can be used instead of serializing the raw data in subsequent packets.
requirements: incr must be a valid pointer to the instance’s incremental state.
type must be a valid field id in perfetto.protos.InternedData (int32 identifier).
data must point to the raw bytes that uniquely identify the value to intern (may be any byte sequence, including a serialized protobuf or small integer encoding).
data_size must be the exact size in bytes of the memory region pointed to by data; if data_size is zero, behavior is unknown (not documented).
seen must be a non-NULL pointer to a bool to receive whether the value was previously interned for this type.
Callers should use the returned iid in place of the raw data when emitting subsequent packets.

import random
import struct
import zlib

# Target data type: arbitrary binary data
# Produce up to 4096 bytes of interesting but valid raw bytes.

_MAX_OUT = 4096

def _well_known_chunks():
    return [
        b"",
        b"\x00" * 32,
        b"\xff" * 32,
        bytes(range(256)),
        bytes(reversed(range(256))),
        b"Perfetto\x00SDK\x00",
        b"protobuf\x82\x01varint\x00\x80\x80\x80\x80\x10",
        struct.pack("<Q", 0x0123456789ABCDEF),
        struct.pack("<I", 0x89ABCDEF),
        struct.pack("<d", 3.141592653589793),
        struct.pack("<f", 1.0),
        b"A" * 127,
        b"B" * 128,
        b"C" * 255,
        b"D" * 256,
    ]

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    if n <= 0:
        return b""
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _enc_varint(x: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    while True:
        b = x & 0x7F
        x >>= 7
        if x:
            out.append(0x80 | b)
        else:
            out.append(b)
            break
    return bytes(out)

def _structured_varint_block(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a small protobuf-like block.
    val = rng.randrange(0, 1 << 32)
    payload_len = rng.randrange(0, 64)
    payload = _rand_bytes(rng, payload_len)
    out = bytearray()
    out += _enc_varint((1 << 3) | 0)      # field 1, varint
    out += _enc_varint(val)
    out += _enc_varint((2 << 3) | 2)      # field 2, length-delimited
    out += _enc_varint(len(payload))
    out += payload
    return bytes(out)

def _compress_maybe(rng: random.Random, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    if rng.random() < 0.3 and len(data) > 0:
        try:
            return zlib.compress(data)
        except Exception:
            return data
    return data

def _assemble(rng: random.Random, target_len: int | None) -> bytes:
    parts = []
    wk = _well_known_chunks()
    rng.shuffle(wk)
    take = rng.randrange(3, min(8, len(wk)) + 1)
    parts.extend(wk[:take])
    for _ in range(rng.randrange(1, 4)):
        parts.append(_structured_varint_block(rng))
    for _ in range(rng.randrange(2, 6)):
        mode = rng.randrange(5)
        if mode == 0:
            n = rng.randrange(1, 256)
            parts.append(_rand_bytes(rng, n))
        elif mode == 1:
            ch = rng.randrange(256)
            n = rng.randrange(1, 512)
            parts.append(bytes([ch]) * n)
        elif mode == 2:
            rep = rng.randrange(1, 16)
            parts.append((b"\x00\xff" * rep) + (b"\x7f\x80" * rep))
        elif mode == 3:
            n = rng.randrange(16, 128)
            parts.append(bytes(range(n)))
        else:
            s = f"name={rng.randrange(1<<16)};parent={rng.randrange(1<<32)};".encode()
            parts.append(s)
    data = b"".join(parts)
    # Maybe compress a slice
    if len(data) and rng.random() < 0.25:
        start = rng.randrange(0, len(data) + 1)
        end = rng.randrange(start, len(data) + 1)
        comp = _compress_maybe(rng, data[start:end])
        data = data[:start] + comp + data[end:]
    # Fit to target_len if provided
    if target_len is None:
        return data
    if target_len <= 0:
        return b""
    if len(data) > target_len:
        # Safely choose a head length in [0, target_len]
        keep_head = rng.randrange(0, target_len + 1)
        tail_len = target_len - keep_head
        head = data[:keep_head]
        tail = data[-tail_len:] if tail_len > 0 else b""
        return head + tail
    elif len(data) < target_len:
        data += _rand_bytes(rng, target_len - len(data))
    return data

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose an overall size budget, sometimes 0 to exercise degenerate paths.
    choices = [0, 1, 2, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256, 512, 1024, 1536, 2048, 3072, 4096]
    target_len = rng.choice(choices)
    blob = _assemble(rng, target_len)
    if len(blob) > _MAX_OUT:
        blob = blob[:_MAX_OUT]
    return blob

import random
import struct
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets fuzz stubs that consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR() as a C string and
# FUZZ_PARAM(uint64_t) for 64-bit integers. The input format is assumed to be a single
# contiguous byte buffer from which the harness extracts parameters in order.
# We therefore craft a buffer containing multiple interesting NUL-terminated strings
# followed by 64-bit integers to cover different code paths:
# - Varied names (ASCII, UTF-8, long, short, empty)
# - Different parent UUIDs and IDs (0, max, random, patterned)
# The buffer remains <= 4096 bytes.

# Helper to build a C-string (NUL-terminated) ensuring valid UTF-8-like content when desired.
def _make_cstr(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Ensure no embedded NULs before terminator for clean strlen-based consumption.
    data = data.replace(b"\x00", b" ")
    return data + b"\x00"


def _rand_utf8_bytes(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix ASCII and a few multibyte UTF-8 codepoints.
    ascii_chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-./:,@#[](){}" + "\t"
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < length:
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.75:
            out.append(ord(rng.choice(ascii_chars)))
        elif choice < 0.9:
            # 2-byte UTF-8 (U+00A0..U+07FF)
            cp = rng.randint(0x00A0, 0x07FF)
            out.extend(chr(cp).encode('utf-8'))
        else:
            # 3-byte UTF-8 (BMP excluding surrogates)
            while True:
                cp = rng.randint(0x0800, 0xFFFF)
                if not (0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF):
                    break
            out.extend(chr(cp).encode('utf-8'))
    return bytes(out[:length])


def _u64(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<Q', v & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)


def _interesting_u64s(rng: random.Random) -> List[int]:
    vals = [
        0,
        1,
        0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF,
        0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF,
        0x8000000000000000,
        rng.getrandbits(64),
        rng.getrandbits(64),
        # Hash-like patterns
        0xCBF29CE484222325,  # FNV offset basis
        0x100000001B3,       # FNV prime truncated
    ]
    # Shuffle to vary order
    rng.shuffle(vals)
    return vals


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a set of names exercising different lengths and contents.
    names: List[bytes] = []

    # Empty string (becomes just NUL) – valid for c_str()
    names.append(_make_cstr(b""))

    # Short ASCII
    names.append(_make_cstr(b"track"))

    # With punctuation
    names.append(_make_cstr(b"counter:cpu/usage%"))

    # Random ASCII length 32
    names.append(_make_cstr(_rand_utf8_bytes(rng, 32)))

    # Long name near typical limits (256)
    names.append(_make_cstr(_rand_utf8_bytes(rng, 256)))

    # Path-like
    names.append(_make_cstr(b"/proc/self/task/main"))

    # Unicode heavy
    uni = ("Tracevent--".encode('utf-8'))
    names.append(_make_cstr(uni))

    # Deterministic patterned name
    pattern = (b"A" * 63) + b"_name"
    names.append(_make_cstr(pattern))

    # Assemble integers: IDs and parent_uuids pool
    ints = _interesting_u64s(rng)

    # Compose buffer: interleave strings and integers to feed multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM(uint64_t).
    # Many fuzz harnesses read sequentially; we place several pairs to allow reuse across stubs.
    buf = bytearray()

    # Emit a header marker to help any format sniffers (not required, harmless for C-string reads)
    buf.extend(b"TE\x00")

    # Write several name/id/parent combos
    count = min(len(names), 8)
    for i in range(count):
        buf.extend(names[i])
        # For each string, supply two uint64 values: id and parent_uuid
        id_val = ints[i % len(ints)]
        parent_val = ints[(i + 3) % len(ints)]
        buf.extend(_u64(id_val))
        buf.extend(_u64(parent_val))

    # Add a few extra standalone uint64s for consumers that pull more integers
    for v in _interesting_u64s(rng):
        buf.extend(_u64(v))

    # Cap size to 4096
    return bytes(buf[:4096])
